## AI strike affordability (C-8.75E — implemented; live fight and Android read PENDING)

- **Preflight (measured).** Repository root `/app`; branch `development-focus-strategy`; HEAD
  **`dfbff758e9`** — one commit AHEAD of the `211a9a265f` the brief expected (that is C-8.75D's
  commit; `dfbff75` is "Integrate Valéria counter logic and add test suite"), with an **empty**
  `git status --porcelain` before the first edit. The mismatch was verified rather than assumed, and
  nothing was reset, stashed, amended, rebased, committed, pushed, merged or deployed.

- **Root cause, traced in the shipped source rather than taken from the earlier audit.** The
  opponent's in-range decision lived inline in `DuelScene.tsx`'s AI effect and read exactly **one**
  stamina value: `const oppLightCost = getStaminaCost(opp.loadout.weapon, true)`, used by one test,
  `else if (opp.stamina < oppLightCost)`. That test sat BEHIND three branches that could name a
  power attack — `player.isBlocking` (`r < 0.45 ? 'power_attack'`, no stamina test at all),
  `player.health < 25` (`r < 0.7 ? 'quick_attack' : 'power_attack'`), and the standard
  `chooseAIStandardAction(aggression, blockChance)` pool — so an opponent with enough for a light
  attack but not a heavy one threw the heavy anyway. Resolution then billed it with
  `stamina: Math.max(0, prev.stamina - staminaCost)` (two write sites, player and opponent), so the
  shortfall was silently forgiven and the strike was **free**: at 14 SP a 22 SP power slash cost 12
  and kept its full damage. The only other gate in the chain, Goliath's telegraph, already compared
  against `oppHeavyCost` — the correct cost, but only on that one path.

- **The fix, and it is two halves of ONE rule.** New pure module `src/utils/aiActionSelection.ts`
  (no React, no three.js, no storage) exports `canAffordAttack(stamina, weapon, action)` — the cost
  of the attack actually being thrown, with a non-finite stamina affording nothing —
  `enforceAffordableAIAction(action, stamina, weapon)`, and `chooseAITacticalAction(context, rng)`.
  Every cost, threshold, draw count and personality value is untouched: the branch chain was lifted
  out of the scene verbatim (player guarding → power/taunt/block; stamina < light → block/rest;
  player below 25 HP → quick/power; otherwise `chooseAIStandardAction`), and only the RETURNED
  action is passed through the rule.
  1. **Selection** — `DuelScene`'s AI effect now calls `chooseAITacticalAction({ playerIsBlocking,
     playerHealth, stamina: opp.stamina, weapon: opp.loadout.weapon, aggression, blockChance })`.
     An unaffordable power attack becomes the **quick attack it can afford** (the offence, the
     aggression and the turn's shape survive); with neither strike affordable it falls back to the
     existing **`rest`** recovery, so the turn is never wasted on a blow that cannot happen.
  2. **Resolution** — `canAffordAttack(attackerNow.stamina, attackerNow.loadout.weapon, actionType)`
     now sits inside the attack block of `executeCombatTurn`, **beside the C-8.70B §R3 range guard
     and above `resolvingRef.current = true`**. Its refusal is a chronicle line and a return: no
     stamina, no animation, no hit or damage roll, no turn timer. Both checks are necessary: the
     selection guard cannot see the paths that bypass selection — a queued counter, a telegraph
     landing, a stale UI, a direct call — which is exactly what the range guard exists for too.
  3. **The two bypass paths now read the same predicate.** Valéria's queued counter is announced only
     when her quick attack is affordable (otherwise the latch is spent, one line is logged and the
     turn falls through to the ordinary selection, so nothing is left locked), and Goliath's
     telegraph still checks its heavy cost at the moment it queues the landing.

- **Behaviour preserved, deliberately.** No stamina cost, damage formula, hit chance, crit rate,
  defence curve, telegraph/wind-up timing, impact timing, dodge/counter rate, combo or hype value,
  reward, progression value, opponent `aggression`/`blockChance`, HUD layout or collider moved. The
  `Math.max(0, …)` clamps stay (a PAID strike can never go negative); they simply no longer hide an
  unpaid one. The one behavioural change beyond the defect itself: a winded opponent that would have
  thrown a free blow now strikes for what it can afford, rests, or (in the counter case) loses the
  answer — never a free hit, a negative balance or a stalled turn.

- **Regression suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_75E.test.ts` — 37 tests / 724 `expect()` calls.** §A the
  predicate at every boundary the brief names (below the light cost, exactly it, between the costs,
  exactly the power cost, above both), the malformed readings (NaN, ±Infinity, undefined), and every
  weapon in `ITEMS_DB` against its own two costs; §B the downgrade, the `rest` fallback, non-strike
  pass-through and idempotence; §C the PRODUCTION selector across every boundary × every branch × 12
  draws — an attack is always affordable, nothing strikes below the light cost, a power attack is
  never chosen at exactly the light cost, the heavy slice degrades between the costs and is restored
  at the power cost, plus the round trip (the chosen action's cost is payable); §D the shipped
  weights (45/30/25, 60/40, 70/30), the standard branch shown to equal `chooseAIStandardAction`
  exactly, one draw per branch, the malformed-stamina case and every shipped opponent; §E the
  resolution guard and its refusal (spends nothing, hands the turn back); §F the counter, the
  telegraph and the `rest` branch. Sections E and F are ordered source assertions on comment-stripped
  source — this repo has no DOM renderer to mount `<DuelScene/>` under — anchored on CODE markers.

- **`scripts/combatTests.ts` gained four cases** (65 → **69 passed, 0 failed**): both cost boundaries
  on the canonical weapon, every weapon's own costs, the downgrade/fallback, and a 6 × 2 × 2 × 8
  boundary sweep of the production selector. Both harnesses read the production helpers, not copies.

- **Four existing suites were rebased, not weakened**, because C-8.75E puts a second guard between
  the range guard and the `resolvingRef` commit that their scope pins sliced across:
  `combatActionOrder.test.ts` (§A/§B/§D/§G now slice the range guard's own **brace-balanced** block
  via a new `blockAt()` helper, and the `setIsPlayerTurn(` count is 2 → 3 with a comment naming both

  `combatResponsiveness.test.ts` (§B's `guarded` slice) and `playerWindupCue.test.ts` (§D's count).
  Every assertion those tests make is unchanged — they still prove the RANGE refusal costs nothing —
  and each edit names C-8.75E where a count moved. No assertion was deleted or relaxed.

- **Checks run (2026-10-23, `web` container).** `bun test src/utils/phaseC8_75E.test.ts` → **37 pass /

## AI affordability at resolution (C-8.75F — verification only; live fight and Android still PENDING)

- **Preflight (measured).** Repository root `/app`; branch `development-focus-strategy`; HEAD
  **`38d9d66742`** ("Prevent AI from performing unaffordable strikes", C-8.75E), with an **empty**
  `git status --porcelain` before the first edit. Nothing was reset, stashed, amended, rebased,
  committed, pushed, merged or deployed, and **no production file changed** — the turn's only change
  is the new suite plus this record.

- **Paths traced in the shipped source.** Every route that can resolve an AI attack runs through the
  ONE `executeCombatTurn` in `DuelScene.tsx`, and all four are closed by the C-8.75E guard:
  1. **Ordinary selection** — the AI effect calls `chooseAITacticalAction` (already affordable) and,
     for a strike, `announceEnemyAttack` → production `createPendingStrike` (700 ms) →
     `executeTurnRef.current('opponent', action)`.
  2. **Telegraph impact** — `pendingHeavyAttackRef` → `telegraphLandingRef.current = true` →
     `executeCombatTurn('opponent', 'power_attack')` (the marker is read-and-cleared at the top, so a
     refusal cannot leave it set).
  3. **Valéria's queued counter** — `pendingCounterRef` → `canAffordAttack(..., 'quick_attack')` →
     `announceEnemyAttack` → the same resolution; an unaffordable counter is dropped and the turn
     falls through to ordinary selection.
  4. **Direct/stale calls** — the player panel's `executeCombatTurn('player', …)`, and any call that
     skips selection, meet the guard too (it is not gated on the actor).
  **Order verified:** range guard (`isAttackInRange`) → **affordability guard** → `resolvingRef.current
  = true`. Both sit inside `if (isAttackAction)` and above every stamina write, animation, hit/damage
  roll and turn commit, so a refused strike cannot cost stamina, deal damage or schedule a timer.
  **No-lock property verified:** the affordability refusal always releases a non-player actor
  (`setIsExecuting(false)` + `setIsPlayerTurn(true)`) and returns — the state an announced strike
  holds and the state a telegraph landing opens the opponent's turn in.

- **The limitation this suite exists to work around, stated precisely.** `<DuelScene/>` cannot be
  mounted in this repo's tests: there is no DOM renderer (no jsdom, no testing-library) and the
  component mounts a three.js `<Canvas>`, so its `useCallback` closures are unreachable from a test
  harness. C-8.75E's §E therefore asserted the guard's *source order*; it never executed it.

- **What this phase added: `src/utils/phaseC8_75F.test.ts` — 14 tests / 87 `expect()`.** The body of
  the real `executeCombatTurn` (and of `announceEnemyAttack`) is read out of `DuelScene.tsx` at test
  time by a string/comment-aware brace matcher and instantiated with `new Function('env', …)` under
  a `with (env)` scope, so **the executed text is the shipped text** — not a copy, not a
  reimplementation. Every combat formula, `canAffordAttack`, `canResolveStrikeImpact`,
  `queuesCounterOnEvade`/`rollsPassiveEvade`, `shieldGuardStaminaGain`, `HIT_STOP_MS`, `SHAKE_TRAUMA`
  (both parsed from the component) and the pending-strike bookkeeping are the PRODUCTION modules,
  imported. The harness supplies only the React primitives the body touches — `setPlayer`/`setOpp`
  (applied to one object per fighter, mutated in place like the component's state), `setIsExecuting`,
  `setIsPlayerTurn`, `addLog`, `spawnDamageText`, `updateCrowdHype`, the refs, `sounds`/`vibrate`, and
  a fake clock/RNG (`setTimeout`/`clearTimeout`/`performance.now`/`Math.random`). `createPendingStrike`
  is driven through its own documented injectable `timer`, so the 700 ms wind-up is deterministic and
  the suite still exercises the real announce → impact → resolve lifecycle.

- **The failure scenario covered, at the shipped costs** (canonical gladius: light **12** SP, heavy
  **24** SP, so the between-cost balance is 18):
  - **Enough for a light attack, not for a power attack** (18 SP): a forced `power_attack` is
    refused — stamina stays 18, the player's health stays 120, **no damage number of any kind** (not
    even `MISSED`), `action` stays `idle`, **no turn timer is scheduled**, `resolvingRef` never
    commits, one chronicle line is emitted, and `setIsExecuting(false)` + `setIsPlayerTurn(true)` are
    called once each.
  - **Below the light cost** (11 SP): neither strike resolves, with the same invariants.
  - **Exactly the light cost** (12 SP): `power_attack` refused; `quick_attack` resolves and bills
    exactly 12 (balance 0, never negative).
  - **Malformed/empty balances** (0, −5, `NaN`): refused, balance unchanged (no `NaN` arithmetic).
  - **The player** is held to the same rule on a direct call.
  - **A refused telegraphed landing** consumes `telegraphLandingRef` and adds no hit-stop
    (`freezeUntil` and `trauma` stay 0).
  - **No permanent lock**: after a refusal the very next affordable action in the same harness pays,
    lands and schedules its turn timer.
  - **Paid control** (so the harness is not refusing everything): 100 SP power attack bills exactly
    24, lands, sets its hit-stop, schedules **one** timer, and flushing that 1100 ms timer clears
    `isExecuting`/`resolvingRef` and hands the turn on; a miss (RNG 0.999) still costs 12.
  - **Announced lifecycle end to end**: `announce('power_attack')` at 18 SP → wind-up fires → the
    resolution refuses, the strike is cleared, the turn is handed back, and a following
    `announce('quick_attack')` resolves and bills 12.

## Crowd Momentum milestones (C-8.76B — implemented; the milestone itself NOT observed live)

- **Preflight (measured).** Repository root `/app`; branch `development-focus-strategy`; HEAD
  **`3f83a785deeedd024b77baf327205000b362ef88`** — exactly the C-8.76A audit's baseline — with an
  **empty** `git status --porcelain` before the first edit. Nothing was reset, stashed, amended,
  rebased, committed, pushed, merged or deployed.

- **The gap C-8.76A found, and what this phase gives it.** The combo counter was tracked, shown and
  recorded (`maxCombo`) but changed nothing; hype had exactly one consumer (the purse's crowd-favour
  step). Crowd Momentum now converts every **third consecutive landed player hit** into **+10 hype**,
  through the meter's existing 100-point cap, plus one chronicle line — so the streak is worth
  something to the crowd and nothing at all to the damage formula.

- **The rule is one pure module: `src/utils/crowdMomentum.ts`.** `CROWD_MOMENTUM_INTERVAL` (3),
  `CROWD_MOMENTUM_HYPE_GAIN` (10), `CROWD_HYPE_MAX` (100), `isCrowdMomentumMilestone(count)` (the
  badge's question: is this count 3, 6, 9…?) and `crowdMomentumReward(currentHype, previousCombo,
  comboCount)` → `{ milestone, hypeGain, hype }`. **The award is keyed on the count MOVING FORWARD
  onto a milestone**, never on "the count is a multiple of three": a repeated evaluation (3 → 3), a
  reset (~→ 0) and an unchanged count are all worth 0, which is what makes it idempotent. Malformed
  hype reads as 0 rather than NaN.

- **Where it is read, and why there.** `DuelScene` holds `comboMilestoneRef` and one `useEffect` on
  `[player.comboCount, addLog, updateCrowdHype]` that prices the transition and, only when
  `hypeGain > 0`, calls the existing `updateCrowdHype(() => hype)` (so the peak that pays the purse
  keeps its single writer) and logs `CROWD MOMENTUM! … (+10% Hype)` as a `'crit'` line. The effect
  sits **outside `executeCombatTurn`**, which gives the phase three properties for free and is why
  no second counter, no strike-branch if-check and no new persistent state were needed:
  1. **Player-only by construction.** `player.comboCount` only moves on a player `landed` (+1) or a
     reset (`miss`, `player_damaged`) — an opponent's hit, a taunt, a blocked strike, a dodge or a
     cancelled/unresolved swing cannot produce a forward move, so none can pay.
  2. **Exactly once.** Strict Mode's doubled effect, a re-render and a second identical callback all
     re-observe the same count and pay 0; the C-9 events themselves are untouched (the four
     `applyComboEvent` call sites are byte-identical).
  3. **No turn-path risk.** Nothing is added to the resolution: no damage, hit chance, stamina, AI,
     timing, latch or settlement value moved, so the C-8.71A/B, C-8.75B/E/F guards are unaffected
     (their suites re-run green, unedited).

- **Reset and evade semantics preserved, as the audit asked.** `applyComboEvent` is not changed:
  `landed` +1, `miss` / `player_damaged` / `fully_blocked` → 0, `blocked` / `none` unchanged. An
  **evaded** player strike still leaves the streak standing (production reaches `'none'` by simply
  not calling the helper on the evade branch) and therefore pays nothing — the documented Phase 39B
  behaviour, kept deliberately and pinned in §G of the suite.

- **HUD: the existing badge, lit — no new row, no timer, no layout change.** `CombatHUD` renders the
  same `COMBO ×n` span with the same padding, border width and `animate-pulse`, and swaps only its
  colours when `isCrowdMomentumMilestone(comboCount)` is true (`bg-amber-400/30 border-amber-300
  text-amber-100` + a glow) instead of the shipped orange. A *timed* pulse was rejected: it needs a
  new HUD state and timer and the badge already animates, so the phase lights the badge rather than

## Misassigned hand weights in netfighter and minotaur (C-8.77C — assets repaired; numeric only, Android PENDING)

- **Preflight (measured).** Repository root `/app`; branch `development-focus-strategy`; HEAD
  **`c1b0d6134d`**; `git status --porcelain` **empty** before the first edit. **No C-8.77A/B record
  exists in this file** (those passes were read-only and appended nothing), so the reported defect was
  re-derived from the files themselves with a dependency-free GLB decoder (throwaway scripts in `/tmp`,
  never committed). Nothing was reset, stashed, amended, rebased, committed, pushed, merged or
  deployed, and `public/models/{arena_roman,amazonian,dimachaerus}.glb` are byte-identical.

- **The defect, measured (and it is larger than the audit's estimate).** In `public/models/netfighter.glb`
  **207** vertices — not 154 — and in `public/models/minotaur.glb` **478** — not 108 — carry weights
  `[1, 0, 0, 0]` on joint **6 (`head`)** while the geometry sits on the **back of the hand**. The exact
  count is definition-dependent, so it is measured topologically instead of by radius: every offending
  vertex is a `head`-dominant vertex that shares a mesh edge with 100 %-`hand_l`/`hand_r` surface, and
  the offenders form **four discrete islands per model** (netfighter 97/53/45/12 at |x| 0.661–0.694,
  y 0.498–0.527; minotaur 142/130/108/98 at |x| 0.767–0.824, y 0.522–0.584), 86 / 126 of whose edges
  are an open boundary. Because the binding was rigid to the head, every head rotation dragged the
  patches off the hands: a skinned worst-case edge gap at a welded seam of **0.66–0.77** (netfighter)
  and **0.81–1.01** (minotaur) units on 2.0 / 1.9-unit-tall models, across `Fighting_Idle`, `Defend`,
  `Sword_Attack` and `Hit_Chest`.

- **How the destination bones were chosen — from the mesh, not from a bone's convenience.** Four
  independent lines of evidence agree on the hand (never a finger): (1) every edge leaving an island
  lands on a `hand_l`/`hand_r` vertex and on nothing else — `hand_l` 38/22 neighbours on the two left
  islands, `hand_r` 24/17 on the right, plus one `lowerarm_*` vertex each; (2) the nearest bone
  **segment** is `hand_l`/`hand_r` for all 207 netfighter vertices; on minotaur it is the pinky chain
  for 449 of 478, but that chain's own weighted geometry lies **outboard** of the patch and the patch
  shares no edge with it, so a finger binding would have torn the welds instead of closing them;
  (3) the patches sit **above the palm's own top edge** (netfighter hand max y 0.4977 vs patch 0.4976+;
  minotaur 0.522 vs 0.522+) and **inboard of / at the knuckle line** (netfighter hand max x 0.709 vs
  patch 0.693), i.e. the dorsal metacarpal surface, not a phalanx; (4) binding them to the hand makes
  them **rigid with the surface they are welded to**, so no new deformation can arise.

- **The repair touches only two skinning byte spans.** Each island takes its destination from its own
  welded seam; the one netfighter island with **no** welded edge (12 vertices) uses the dominant bone of
  the nearest correctly weighted hand surface — also `hand_l`. The tool then rewrites, in the BIN chunk
  in place, `JOINTS_0` slot 0 and the four `WEIGHTS_0` bytes of exactly those vertices (u8 weights, so
  `255,0,0,0` = 1.0 exactly). Measured with `cmp -l`, the whole-file difference is **exactly one byte
  per repaired vertex — 207 bytes in `netfighter.glb` and 478 in `minotaur.glb`**: the weights were
  already `255,0,0,0`, so only the joint index byte moved. File size, vertex/triangle data, materials,
  textures, skeleton, inverse-bind matrices and all 178 clips are byte-identical.

  | asset | before sha256 | after sha256 | bytes | verts / joints / clips |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `netfighter.glb` | `f670f441…` | **`a0e0d4dc…`** | 10,670,992 (unchanged) | 106,139 / 56 / 178 |
  | `minotaur.glb` | `0ff529c4…` | **`46dafe41…`** | 9,759,552 (unchanged) | 88,510 / 56 / 178 |

  Repaired vertices: **109 → `hand_l` + 98 → `hand_r`** (netfighter), **240 + 238** (minotaur).

- **Numeric verification (all through the same decoder + glTF skinning the audit used).** Weight sums
  are exactly 1.0 on every vertex of both files (u8, no deviation at all), no invalid joint index, no
  non-finite attribute; bind-pose skinning reproduces the authored geometry to **2.2e-16**; the
  head-dominant totals fall **17,006 → 16,799** and **11,675 → 11,197** and the rigid hand surfaces grow
  by exactly the repaired counts (839 → 948 / 1,167 → 1,265; 553 → 793 / 561 → 799). Against the four
  named clips, evaluated on a harness normalised for the asset's own **0.9482× / 0.9500× hierarchy-vs-
  IBM scale mismatch** (a pre-existing asset property, unrelated to this phase), the welded-seam
  deviation drops from **0.66–0.77 / 0.81–1.01** to **exactly 0** (netfighter) and **0.006–0.036**
  (minotaur) — and that minotaur residual is the asset's **own pre-existing wrist blend**: the control
  set of untouched `hand`↔`lowerarm` seams deviates by 0.013–0.057 in *both* files before and after.
  Every interior patch triangle keeps **0 % area change** (no collapse, no stretch); the patch's
  distance to the palm stays exactly at its authored offset (0 deviation both models). Nothing was
  gained by binding to a finger and a great deal would have been lost.

- **Shared fused-finger defect — diagnosed, deliberately NOT edited.** The hands are **not** one fused
  slab: the hand region is **29** separate shells in each model (26 in `arena_roman`), but the weights
  are a hard partition — **282** (netfighter) / **426** (minotaur) / **121** (`arena_roman`) shared
  edges carry a >0.5 L2 weight jump while **zero** vertices blend two chains, and most of a hand is
  driven by one or two chains (`index` has **no** dominant vertices at all in netfighter and minotaur).
  Rotating those chains therefore stretches the seams by up to **0.094 / 0.153** units. A minimal
  correction (blending one or two edge rings across the hard steps) is plausible, but it would spread
  the deformation into the surrounding surface and change the silhouette under motion, so it needs its
  own numeric **and device** validation — reported, not attempted. `arena_roman`, `amazonian` and
  `dimachaerus` are untouched and provably free of the head-assignment defect (0 offenders each).

- **Regression suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_77c.test.ts` — 15 tests / 1,453 `expect()`.** §A the two files
  byte-for-byte **plus** their vertex/joint/clip counts and skeleton names (a re-export must re-run the
  audit); §B per side, the measured patch box contains **no** `head`-dominant vertex, still holds
  exactly 109 / 98 and 240 / 238 vertices, and every one is rigid to the correct hand; §C weight hygiene
  over every vertex, the head/rigid-hand totals; §D the three untouched models' hashes; §E controls —
  re-binding either patch to `head` in memory is caught on both counts, so the guard is shown sensitive
  to the defect rather than merely green.

- **Checks run (2026-10-23, `web` container).** `bun test src/utils/phaseC8_77c.test.ts` → **15 pass /
  0 fail** (1,453 `expect()`); with the two suites that inventory `public/models`
  (`phaseC8_67d`, `phaseC8_68c`) → **86 pass / 0 fail**; `bun run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) → **exit 0**;
  `git diff --check` → clean. The full `bun test` sweep was deliberately not run (sandbox CPU is shared
  with the preview); no existing suite pins these two files' contents, only the directory listing.

- **Live evidence, and its limit.** In the preview browser (anonymous visitor) the app's own model
  loading path was driven — title → character creation → **The Retiarius** and then **Minotaur** — and
  both repaired files were fetched by `useGLTF` at **HTTP 200** (10,670,992 and 9,755,952 bytes), with
  each model rendering on its platform and **0 console errors / 0 failed requests**. That proves the
  files parse and load through the shipping path; it is **not visual acceptance**. **Device check owed:**
  on Android, watch a netfighter and a minotaur in idle/attack/hit and confirm the back-of-hand spikes
  are gone and no seam opens at the wrist, and confirm the hands still read as hands rather than
  flattened plates.

- **Restoration.** The pre-repair bytes are recoverable from git (`git checkout <pre-phase commit> --
  public/models/netfighter.glb public/models/minotaur.glb`); copies were also kept outside the repo in
  `/tmp/handfix/backup/` with the before hashes recorded above. No commit, push, merge or deployment was
  made by this phase; the asset change plus the suite and this record are the whole diff.

## Crowd Momentum reward accuracy and hit-stop pins (Phase C-8.78B — implemented)

- **The defect was the chronicle, not the mechanic.** `crowdMomentumReward` returned the NOMINAL
  milestone value (`hypeGain: 10`) alongside the capped meter reading (`hype: 100`), and
  `DuelScene`'s combo effect printed `+${hypeGain}% Hype` from that pair — so a milestone reached at
  hype 100 announced a 10-point gain while the meter correctly stayed at 100 (C-8.78A §D1).
- **The correction is one derived field plus one string.** The helper now also returns
  `hypeAwarded = hype - safeHype`, i.e. the meter's real movement after the 100-point cap; the
  caller destructures it, keeps the `if (hypeGain === 0) return;` milestone gate and the single
  `updateCrowdHype` write, and logs `+${hypeAwarded}% Hype`. A zero award gets its own line instead
  of a false claim: "CROWD MOMENTUM! N unanswered strikes — the mob is on its feet, but the Hype is
  already at its full 100%." `hypeGain` keeps its nominal meaning (so `phaseC8_76` §E's
  `hypeGain === 10` at the cap still holds); the interval, the +10 threshold, the cap, the combo
  transition rule, the gold payout and every combat formula are untouched.
- **Regression suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_78b.test.ts`** — 36 tests / 721 assertions in nine
  sections: §A normal gains, §B partial gains near the ceiling (95 → +5, 99.5 → +0.5, with an
  `awarded + previous === hype` sweep), §C the zero award at the cap (milestone still true, award 0,
  over-cap readings clamped first), §D the shipped caller (one evaluation, `hypeAwarded` in the
  line, no `(+${hypeGain}% Hype)`, the truthful zero branch, gate/write order unchanged), §E the
  five `HIT_STOP_MS` holds pinned at 40 / 60 / 110 / 170 / 200 with their key set and severity
  order, §F the heavy-minus-quick delta of 140 pinned as a DERIVATION (no configured hold is 140,
  no key claims to be), §G the blocked → telegraphed heavy → crit → quick → power precedence and the
  landed-vs-received trauma rule evaluated through `new Function` on the extracted expressions,
  §H `SHAKE_TRAUMA` (0.25 / 0.45 / 0.7 / 0.2), the `Math.min(1, …)` accumulation and the camera's
  0.18 / 0.6° / 1.6 u/s response, and §I `impactAnimationScale` driven on an injected clock
  (0 strictly before `freezeUntil`, 1 at and after it) plus its two wiring sites in `GladiatorMesh`.
  Extraction is regex/brace-match based and evaluated as real expressions, so reformatting the
  constant blocks cannot fail it — only a rename, deletion or value drift can.
- **Mutation-checked, both restored byte-for-byte (`sha256sum -c` clean):** heavy hold 200 → 20 →
  3 tests fail; caller printing `hypeGain` → 1 fails; `hypeAwarded: hypeGain` (ignoring the cap) →
  8 fail.
- **Verified 2026-10-23** in the dev container: focused `bun test src/utils/phaseC8_78b.test.ts` →
  **36 pass / 0 fail**; with `phaseC8_76` → **63 pass / 0 fail** (865 expect()); broader combat
  (`combatResponsiveness`, `phaseC8_75B`, `phaseC8_75F`, `playerStrikeWindup`, `pendingStrike`,
  `playerWindupCue`) → **135 pass / 0 fail**; `bun test` → **3440 pass / 0 fail (119 files,
  92,143 expect())** (C-8.78A left 3404 / 118; the delta is this suite); `bun run lint`
  (`tsc --noEmit`) → exit 0; `git diff --check` → clean. The dev server transforms both edited
  modules (`/src/utils/crowdMomentum.ts` and `/src/components/duel/DuelScene.tsx` → HTTP 200, with
  `hypeAwarded: hype - safeHype` present in the served module).
- **Not automatically verified — the rendered chronicle line.** No duel was driven to hype 100 in
  the preview (the duel renders through SwiftShader at a few fps and reaching the cap needs ~10

## Out-of-range attack fairness (Phase C-8.79A — audit, no production change)

- **The shipped path already satisfies the contract, so no production file was touched.** The whole
  player attack path was traced at `e9628b0a5e`: the tactic panel's `onExecuteAction` is the single
  player entry (`DuelScene.tsx` has exactly one `executeCombatTurn('player', …)` call and no
  keyboard/touch second path) → `executeCombatTurn` → the `resolvingRef`/`isMatchOver` latch → the
  telegraphed-heavy read-and-clear → the **range guard** → the C-8.75E affordability guard → the
  `resolvingRef` commit and `setIsExecuting(true)` → the attack branch's stamina spend and swing
  animation → `playerStrikeRef.current?.strike(...)` (the 700 ms pending strike) → `resolveImpact`,
  which re-checks `canResolveStrikeImpact` → the 1100 ms turn timer. **The range guard precedes all
  of it**, and its refusal block contains only `addLog(…)` and `return;` — no stamina write, no
  fighter mutation, no pending strike, no `resolveImpact`, no timer.
- **One range rule, measured.** `isAttackInRange(distance, weapon)` accepts `distance <= weapon.range`
  (boundary legal: the starting gladius' 2.1 is in range, 2.1001 is not; non-finite/negative/≤0 reach
  is refused). The engine's `gap` and the HUD's `currentDistance` are the *same* expression,
  `Math.abs(player.position[2] - opp.position[2])`, so the panel cannot disagree with the guard.
- **A duel starts out of range and the panel is coherent there.** Spawn positions are Z ±3.5, i.e.
  distance 7.0 against 2.1 — so at the opening bell both strikes are disabled with
  `Out of range — Advance to strike`, **Advance is enabled** (it is disabled *in* range, which is
  what stops the fighters being walked through each other), Retreat is enabled below 9.0, and Shield
  Guard / Dodge / Taunt / Rest are unaffected. Every duel therefore exercises the out-of-range state
  from the first frame.
- **Coverage gap filled by `src/utils/phaseC8_79A.test.ts`** (11 tests, 75 `expect()`), the only file
  this phase adds: §A pins the refusal *before* the pending-strike dispatch and the turn timer and the
  refusal block's mutation-free body, plus the single player entry point; §B pins the shared distance
  expression through `CombatHUD` to `TurnActionPanel`; §C **renders the shipped panel** with
  `react-dom/server` (the repo's first executable UI check of this rule) and asserts the buttons
  themselves: just outside reach and at 7.5 both strikes are `disabled` with the overlay, at the 2.1
  boundary and at 1.2 they are enabled with no overlay, low stamina out of range is still disabled,
  and out of range the **Advance** card is the enabled remedy while in range it is the disabled one.
  Off-turn and mid-resolution both strikes are disabled inside reach too.
- **Mutation evidence (each restored and `cmp`-verified byte-for-byte).** Bypassing the engine guard
  (`if (false && !isAttackInRange(…))`) fails 4 tests across `phaseC8_79A`, `combatActionOrder`,
  `combatResponsiveness` and `playerStrikeWindup` (plus 2 file-level errors from the missing
  anchor). Removing `|| !isInWeaponRange` from the quick-strike button fails 4 tests — 3 of them the
  rendered §C checks, i.e. the render catches a gate edit the source-count pin also happens to catch.
- **Verified 2026-10-19** in the dev container: focused `bun test src/utils/phaseC8_79A.test.ts` →
  **11 pass / 0 fail**; the adjacent combat set (`combatActionOrder`, `combatResponsiveness`,

## Opponent readability and reaction-window audit (Phase C-8.79B — audit + one fix)

- **Preflight (measured).** Repository root `/app`; branch `development-focus-strategy`; HEAD
  **`8eeff15829`** with an **empty** `git status --porcelain` before the first edit. Nothing was
  reset, stashed, discarded, amended, rebased, committed, pushed, merged or deployed. Final HEAD is
  unchanged (`8eeff15829`) — this phase's work is the working tree plus **this section**.

- **The lifecycle, traced in the shipped source (exact values and guard locations).**
  1. **Selection + affordability.** The AI effect (`DuelScene.tsx`, `setTimeout(…, 750)`) only runs
     when `!isPlayerTurn && !isExecuting && !isMatchOver.current && opp.health > 0`. In range it calls
     `chooseAITacticalAction` (`utils/aiActionSelection`), whose every strike passes through
     `enforceAffordableAIAction` → `canAffordAttack` — the cost of the attack **actually thrown**
     (gladius: light **12** SP, heavy **24** SP), a non-finite stamina affording nothing. Out of range
     it calls `chooseAIOutOfRangeAction` (advance/taunt), which can never name a strike.
  2. **Announcement.** A chosen strike goes to `announceEnemyAttack`, never to resolution. That sets
     `strikeRef.current.announce(action, onImpact)` (`utils/pendingStrike`,`ENEMY_ATTACK_WINDUP_MS =
     **700**`), `setPendingEnemyAttack(action)`, `setReactionTaken(null)`, `setIsExecuting(true)` (the
     HUD lock for the whole window), the opponent's swing animation, and one chronicle line. A second
     announce inside the window is refused by `announce` and returns before any state is written.
  3. **Reaction window.** The cue (`CombatHUD`, `data-windup-cue`) renders on the same React update as
     the announcement; its bar is `animationDuration: ${ENEMY_ATTACK_WINDUP_MS}ms` (700), so the drawn
     window and the timer read the **same** constant. `reactToPendingAttack` refuses a dodge below
     `DODGE_STAMINA_COST` (**12**) **before** claiming, then `claimReaction()` (at most once per
     announcement) **before** writing either stance.
  4. **Resolution of the answer.** Dodge → `isInvulnerable`; Shield Guard → `isBlocking`. The impact
     reads `defender.isInvulnerable && Math.random() < 0.75` for the evade and
     `defender.isBlocking` → `blockReduction` for the guard, i.e. the two stances meet the existing
     rules; the turn-end reset preserves both flags (`resolveTurnEndDefensive`) so they survive into
     the incoming strike.
  5. **Impact and turn.** The impact fires `executeTurnRef.current('opponent', landing)` — the
     **latest** resolution closure, so a stance raised during the cue is what the blow meets. It meets
     the same `executeCombatTurn` guards in order: `resolvingRef`/`isMatchOver` →
     telegraphed-heavy read-and-clear → **range** (`isAttackInRange`) → **affordability**
     (`canAffordAttack`) → `resolvingRef = true` / `setIsExecuting(true)` → the stamina bill → the
     swing → `resolveImpact`, which re-checks `canResolveStrikeImpact`. The turn ends on the shared
     **1100 ms** timer, which is longer than the 700 ms wind-up, so an impact can never run after the
     turn has moved on.
  6. **Settlement and cancellation.** `isMatchOver` is latched in the outcome effect **before** the
     1400 ms settlement is scheduled; both outcome branches clear `pendingHeavyAttackRef` /
     `pendingCounterRef` and call `cancelPendingEnemyAttack()`; the impact callback re-checks
     `isMatchOver` before resolving; and the unmount cleanup clears the turn timer and cancels both
     controllers (`strikeRef`, `playerStrikeRef`). Valéria's queued counter is consumed
     (`pendingCounterRef.current = false`) **before** it is announced, and she is re-checked for
     affordability there, so it can neither resolve twice nor survive a stale turn.

- **The one defect, and it was a UI/state discrepancy rather than a mechanics one.** The reaction cue
  was **stance-blind**: `reactionTaken` was a boolean and the line under the telegraph read
  *"Stance set — the strike lands against your guard."* whichever answer was given. After a **Dodge**
  that is false twice over — `reactToPendingAttack('dodge')` sets `isInvulnerable` and never
  `isBlocking`, the impact rolls the 75 % evade, and a failed roll lands at **full** damage because no
  guard was raised. So the only feedback inside a 700 ms decision window told the player their shield
  was up when it was not. **Reproduction, in the shipped HUD** (the dev harness mounts the real
  component): `/?devHarness=hud&hudState=power` → press `Dodge` → `data-hud-reacts="dodge"` while the
  cue read the guard line.

- **The fix is the stance, one rule and one line — no combat value moved.** `reactionTaken` is now
  `PendingReaction | null` (`'shield_block' | 'dodge'`): `DuelScene` writes `setReactionTaken(action)`
  after the claim (unchanged order) and clears it to `null` at announce, at impact and in
  `cancelPendingEnemyAttack`; `utils/pendingStrike` gains `resolveReactionCue(reaction)` — the same
  module that already owns the announcement/reaction bookkeeping — returning
  *"Dodge set — a chance to slip the blow entirely."* or *"Guard set — the blow lands at reduced
  force."*; `CombatHUD` renders that label and exposes `data-reaction-kind` beside the existing
  `data-reaction-taken`. The dev harness passes the reaction it actually delivered. **Untouched:**
  every stamina cost, damage formula, hit chance, dodge rate (still the inline 0.75), wind-up (700),
  hit-stop, shake, turn timer (1100), AI delay (750), Crowd Momentum, rewards, the announcement API,
  the claim ordering and every opponent's data.

- **Scenario results (evidence named for each).**

  | scenario | status | evidence |
  |---|---|---|
  | a normal opponent attack gives the documented window | **PASS** | 700 ms constant read by both the controller and the drawn bar; `pendingStrike` §A (nothing lands before the wind-up, the impact carries the announced action) |
  | rapid input cannot bypass or duplicate the lifecycle | **PASS** | `claimReaction` once per announcement (`pendingStrike` §B), a second `announce` refused (§C), the cue's two controls are replaced after the claim — re-read live in this phase |
  | dodge and block meet the telegraphed strike consistently | **PASS** | source trace: `isInvulnerable` → 75 % evade, `isBlocking` → `blockReduction`; the flags are preserved by `resolveTurnEndDefensive` (`defensiveBalance`) |
  | Valéria's counter resolves at most once | **PASS** | latch consumed pre-announce + `canAffordAttack` re-check; `phaseC8_75B` §A, the C-8.75D source guard |
  | unaffordable strikes are neither selected nor charged | **PASS** | `enforceAffordableAIAction` at selection and `canAffordAttack` at resolution (`phaseC8_75E`/`phaseC8_75F`) |
  | a bout ending during a pending strike prevents late damage/counters | **PASS** | both branches cancel before settling and the callback re-checks the latch (`duelResultLifecycle` §D) |
  | leaving the duel prevents delayed effects | **PASS (source + suite)** | the unmount cleanup cancels both controllers (`duelResultLifecycle` §D). **Not driven live**: the only leaves are the HUD's Armory badge and the result screen, neither reached in this pass |
  | announcements and impacts are the same pending strike | **PASS** | the impact passes the controller's own `landing`, read at impact time (`pendingStrike` §A) |
  | **the reaction cue reports the stance taken** | **FAIL → FIXED** | the defect above, reproduced in the shipped HUD and re-checked live after the fix |

- **Two timing notes a future phase should not re-derive.** (1) The player's window is **700 ms
  measured from the announcement**, which itself follows the AI effect's **750 ms** think delay — so
  the opponent's whole turn reads as ~1450 ms before the blow. (2) On a slow device the cue can mount
  late relative to the timer (React commits the state it was written in, while the 700 ms timer is
  wall-clock), so the *visible* window can be shorter than the configured one; that is a
  hardware question, not a source inconsistency, and it is unmeasurable in this sandbox.

- **Files changed (one defect, no balance change).** `src/utils/pendingStrike.ts` (the
  `PendingReaction` type and `resolveReactionCue`), `src/components/ui/CombatHUD.tsx` (prop typed to
  the union, the resolved label, `data-reaction-kind`), `src/components/duel/DuelScene.tsx` (the state
  carries the stance; four write sites), `src/components/dev/CombatHudHarness.tsx` (passes the
  delivered reaction), `src/utils/combatResponsiveness.test.ts` (**two pins rebased, none weakened** —
  the prop's type and the write's argument, each with a comment naming this phase), and the new
  `src/utils/phaseC8_79B.test.ts` (16 tests / 45 `expect()`: §A the rule, §B the **rendered** HUD for
  both stances, §C the shipped write sites and the claim-before-write order, §D the untouched
  lifecycle).

- **Mutation evidence (each restored and `sha256sum -c` clean).** Reverting the cue to the old
  stance-blind line (`{reactionCue.label}` → the fixed guard string) fails **exactly** `§B — after a
  Dodge the cue does not claim a raised guard` (1 fail / 15 pass); reverting the write to
  `setReactionTaken(true)` fails **exactly** `§C — the reaction writes the stance it was handed` and
  the claim-before-write pin (2 fail / 14 pass). With both restored, all 16 pass.

- **Checks run (2026-10-23, `web` container, on the final tree).** Focused combat set
  `{pendingStrike, combatActionOrder, combatResponsiveness, phaseC8_75B, phaseC8_75F, defensiveBalance,
  duelResultLifecycle, phaseC8_79A, phaseC8_79B}` → **172 pass / 0 fail** (764 `expect()`, 9 files);
  full `bun test` → **3467 pass / 0 fail (121 files, 92,263 `expect()`)** — C-8.79A left 3451 / 120, the
  delta being this suite's 16 tests and its file; `bun run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) → **exit 0**;
  `git diff --check` → **clean**.

- **Live evidence (preview browser, anonymous visitor — no session replayed).** The shipped HUD was

- **Not automatically verified — do not read the table above as covering it.** No duel was fought in

  **Android acceptance stays PENDING** for the whole reaction surface: that the cue is readable at

## Weapon attachment and reach calibration (C-8.80E — implemented; runtime transforms measured, device read PENDING)

- **No C-8.80D record exists in this repo** (that audit was read-only), so the defect was re-derived
  from the assets and the code. Full record: [.base44/weapon-attachment-c880e.md](.base44/weapon-attachment-c880e.md).
- **The proven defect: the weapon was the only bone-attached item that did not divide the body
  correction back out.** `GladiatorMesh`'s root group carries `scale = meshScale ×
  MODEL_SCALE_CORRECTIONS[characterModel]`; the shield compensates (`SHIELD_SCALE_GLB / modelCorrection`,
  0.6095 world height on every body) but the weapon inherited it, so the *same* 1.000-unit gladius
  rendered **1.000** on `arena_roman` (correction 1.00) and **0.610 / 0.600 / 0.770** on
  amazonian / dimachaerus / minotaur. Combat reach is world-space, so those bodies struck 23-40 %
  short: at the legal gladius range `dimachaerus`' `Sword_Attack` came **0.904** from the defender's
  nearest vertex against **0.515** corrected.
- **The fix is one attachment group, inside the hand bone.** New pure `src/utils/weaponAttachment.ts`
  (`attachmentScaleForModelCorrection(correction) = 1/correction`, total) and
  `const weaponAttachment = <group scale={weaponAttachmentScale}>{weaponNode}</group>`, used by
  **both** hands. Composition is `meshScale × correction × (1/correction) = meshScale`, so a boss at
  `meshScale 1.25` still swings a 1.25-length weapon. The shield's expression, the fighter root, its
  ground alignment, `getWeaponRange`, damage, stamina, hit timing, AI and the settlement are untouched.
- **Explicitly NOT changed, because the measurements did not support it:** no multiplier was applied to
  `arena_roman` (1.000 units against 1.101 of rendered height is already 91 %), and the residual
  standoff shortfall present on *every* body (0.515 corrected at 2.1) is the character's ~1.10-unit
  world scale plus the clip's contact frame at ~0.56-0.69 s against a 0.70 s resolution — the open
  "models render at ~60 % intended height" issue and the hit-timing rule, both out of scope. A future
  phase that widens visible reach further must fix the body's world scale or the clip, not the weapon.
- **Suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_80e.test.ts`** (16 tests / 49 expect(), ~0.35 s) — runtime-transform
  assertions over the real GLBs (weapon world length equal on both bodies, `meshScale` still applied,
  attachment parented to `hand_r`, shield height and posed ground offset unchanged, combat constants
  and the 2.1 range boundary pinned, both hands binding the one node), plus a control showing the
  pre-fix render is 0.4 shorter. Removing the wrapper fails it.
- **Verified 2026-10-24** in the `web` container: focused suite 16/0; focused combat set **241/0**;
  `bun run scripts/combatTests.ts` **69/0**; `bun test` **3531 pass / 0 fail (124 files, 92,562
  expect())**; `bun run lint` exit 0; `git diff --check` clean. Preview: title screen and the dev
  character harness mount (creation preview renders the Roman Warrior with sword and shield, one
  canvas, **0 console errors**), which proves the extra attachment group renders through
  `createPortal`.
- **Not automatically verified:** the corrected blade *reading* as reaching further on the four
  alternative bodies in a live bout (SwiftShader duel ~1-2 fps cannot adjudicate 0.4 units), and the
  residual standoff shortfall above. **Android acceptance remains PENDING** — do not claim device or
  visual acceptance.

## Attack contact-phase calibration (C-8.80G — implemented; clip timing measured, duel frame PENDING)

- **The defect, re-measured because no C-8.80F record exists in this repo.** The player's swing is
  committed at the tap and damage resolves one fixed `PLAYER_ATTACK_WINDUP_MS` (700 ms) later, but
  the clips were authored without that window: with the real assets through a real `AnimationMixer`
  and the shipped hierarchy (the C-8.80E attachment included), `Sword_Attack`'s blade tip reaches
  its closest approach to the defender at **519 ms** and `Sword_Regular_C`'s at **659 ms**. At the
  700 ms impact the tip is 2.032 and 1.673 from the defender against 0.786 and 0.573 at contact —
  the blade has visibly left the target before the number appears.
- **Per clip, not per model and not a universal multiplier.** All five shipped bodies load the same
  178 clips and `resolveActionClip` resolves the same two attack clips on every one; re-measuring
  each body (amazonian 0.61, dimachaerus 0.60, minotaur 0.77, netfighter 0.60) puts contact within
  **6 ms** (517-523 / 659-661). The two clips differ by 140 ms, so one constant per clip is the
  right granularity.
- **The fix is one module and one line.** `src/utils/attackContact.ts` holds the two measured contact
  times and derives `rate = contact / window`, where the window is the 700 ms wind-up with two
  one-frame offsets that **cancel**: the clip's clock starts a frame after the commit (the action
  effect runs post-commit and the mixer advances next frame), and the hit-stop holds the pose
  sampled a frame *after* the impact (`GladiatorMesh` sets `mixer.timeScale = 0` in a `useFrame`
  that runs after drei's mixer update). Rates: `Sword_Attack` **0.7414**, `Sword_Regular_C`
  **0.9414**. `GladiatorMesh`'s action effect applies
  `nextAction.setEffectiveTimeScale(attackPlaybackRateForAction(activeAction, targetClip))` after
  `reset()` (which does not clear the rate), for both fighters. `mixer.timeScale` stays the
  hit-stop's only channel — the file still has exactly one assignment to it — and every non-striking
  action still plays at 1.
- **Left at the better end of the one-frame band, deliberately.** The freeze pose is sampled
  somewhere within one frame of the impact; a frame *after* contact costs less than a frame *before*
  it on both clips (517→533 ms: 0.790→0.912; 650→667 ms: 0.892→0.792), so contact is aligned to the
  impact rather than biased early.
- **Explicitly not changed:** both 700 ms wind-ups, the 1100 ms turn window, the `HIT_STOP_MS` table
  (60/110/170/40/200), damage, range, stamina, the AI, the defensive stances, the withdrawal path,
  the settlement and the C-8.80E weapon attachment. Cancellation and withdrawal still drop the
  pending swing (`playerStrike.cancel()` in both paths, pinned in the suite).
- **Suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_80g.test.ts`** (22 tests / 92 expect(), ~0.6 s) — rate derivation and
  per-clip values, contact frames re-measured from the real GLBs (arena_roman and minotaur, within
  7 ms), real `AnimationAction` semantics (`action.time` at the impact, the hit-stop holding it,
  resumption at `rate × delta`), the unchanged combat contract, and cancellation/withdrawal.
  `bun test` **3553 pass / 0 fail (125 files, 92,654 expect())**, `bun run lint` exit 0,
  `git diff --check` clean. Full record: [.base44/attack-contact-c880g.md](.base44/attack-contact-c880g.md).
- **Not automatically verified:** a live duel capture at the impact frame — the sandbox renders the
  duel through SwiftShader at ~1-2 fps against a 700 ms window, so the comparison comes from the
  deterministic transform harness. **Android visual acceptance remains PENDING**; the residual ~0.5
  world-unit standoff at the legal range (C-8.80E) is untouched.

## Accurate movement reports (C-8.80K — implemented; normal and clamped lines verified live)

- **The defect was the chronicle, not the movement.** Advance printed "advances 1.8m toward their
  opponent" and Retreat "retreats back 1.8m" whatever the clamps did: at the 1.2 m minimum gap an
  Advance does not move at all, and at the ±7.5 m arena edge a Retreat is shortened and then refused
  — so a fighter at grips was told they had walked. `DuelScene` already computed the clamped target
  (`utils/duelGeometry`, C-8.80J); only the sentence ignored it.
- **The fix is one pure module plus one reading of the real positions.** `src/utils/duelMoveReport.ts`
  exports `moveDisplacement(fromZ, toZ)`, `reportedDistance` (one decimal — the shipped precision),
  `formatMoveDistance` ("1.8m") and `describeMoveReport(name, action, fromZ, toZ)`, which answers the
  full sentence (verbatim as shipped), `advances only 0.8m … — the enemy is already at grips.`,
  `cannot advance — the enemy is already at grips.`, and the retreat pair `retreats only 1.5m — the
  arena's edge stops them.` / `cannot retreat — the arena's edge is at their back.` Rounding happens
  ONCE, on the same value the "did they move" decision uses, so a sub-0.05 m float residual reads as
  no movement rather than "0.0m". `DuelScene`'s two movement branches now read `fromZ =
  attacker.position[2]` before computing `targetZ`, and log through the helper. **Player and
  opponent share that one path**, so the AI's step is fixed by the same change.
- **What did not move:** the 1.8 m step, the 1.2 m minimum gap, the ±7.5 m limit, the C-8.80J 3.6 m
  opening, the `resolve*TargetZ` call sites (still two each), the `walk` action, the stamina rule,
  the wind-up/turn timings and every combat value. The tactic card's "Advance (+1.8m)" label is the
  ACTION's nominal description, not a performed step, and was deliberately left alone.
- **Suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_80k.test.ts`** (17 tests / 52 expect()) — the seven required outcomes
  driven through the shipped helpers and the shipped formatter (unobstructed advance, gap-clamped
  advance, refused advance, ordinary retreat, edge-clamped retreat, refused retreat), the opponent
  mirror, the formatting/rounding rules, and the wiring pins (helper used in both branches, no flat
  "1.8m" claim left in code, clamps/values/stamina untouched, no timer or randomness in the branch).
  Mutation-checked: restoring the flat advance literal fails 3 of the 17 (`sha256sum -c` clean after).
- **Verified 2026-10-24** in the `web` container: focused suite 17/0; the movement+combat set
  (`phaseC8_80j`, `phaseC8_80k`, `combatActionOrder`, `combatResponsiveness`, `phaseC8_79A`) →
  **98 pass / 0 fail**; `bun run scripts/combatTests.ts` → **69 passed, 0 failed**; `bun test` →
  **3590 pass / 0 fail (127 files, 92,791 expect())**; `bun run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) → exit 0;
  `git diff --check` → clean.
- **Live evidence (preview browser, anonymous visitor, the dev duel harness in an in-page frame).**
  One Advance logged **"Spartacus advances 1.8m toward their opponent."**; the opponent's own step
  logged **"Marcus the Rookie advances 1.8m toward their opponent."**; and four retreats at 1.8 m
  each plus the fifth, from z 7.2 to the 7.5 edge, logged **"Spartacus retreats only 0.3m — the
  arena's edge stops them."** — the clamp reported at the distance actually travelled, read from the
  running chronicle. The frame was removed afterwards (`leakedFrames: 0`); the harness writes nothing.
- **Not verified live:** the two REFUSED lines (a further retreat at the edge, and an Advance at the
  1.2 m gap) — reaching them needs more turns than the script budget allowed at SwiftShader's
  ~1–2 fps; both are unit-verified. **Android acceptance is PENDING** for how the longer clamped
  sentences wrap in the five-line chronicle on a phone.

## Phone duel composition (Phase C-8.80N — implemented; live geometry measured, device read PENDING)

- **The defect was composition, not camera and not combat.** The duel's canvas was full-viewport and the HUD
  was an overlay on top of it, so the bottom panel sat exactly where the two fighters project. Measured live
  at 400x800: the top block ended at y 227, the stacked chronicle began at y 290 and the tactic dashboard
  ended at y 818, while the cinematic camera put the opponent at 341-427 and the player at 506-616 in the
  same 800px canvas — **both fighters were entirely behind HUD chrome.** With the rig's fixed vertical FOV
  the fighters project to the same *fraction* of canvas height at every width (opponent 42.6%-53.4%, player
  63.3%-77.0% at the 3.6m opening), so no amount of chrome-shedding could help: the canvas had to stop being
  covered.
- **What ships now.** `DuelScene` renders a `.duel-stage` (canvas + the instrumentation HUD that overlays it)
  and a `.duel-command` panel as **siblings**; `TurnActionPanel` therefore left `CombatHUD` (its five props
  moved with it, and `CombatHUD`'s root lost `justify-between`, which would otherwise push the zero-height
  cue wrappers to the stage's bottom). `index.css` carries the default (desktop/tablet) placement —
  stage `absolute inset-0`, panel absolute across the bottom at the same 20px/16px insets as before, so the
  established layout is untouched — plus two phone blocks: portrait (`max-width: 520px` + portrait) stacks
  the stage above the panel; short landscape (`orientation: landscape` + `max-height: 520px`) puts the panel
  in a 460px right-hand column beside it. Compaction is chrome only (shortened vital bars via
  `.vital-health-bar`/`.vital-stamina-bar`, a one-line crowd meter, the utility row's `data-hud-label` text
  hidden with the icons and their `title`s kept, tactic blurbs hidden, the chronicle list capped but still

  three. **No control was removed or resized, and no camera, combat, canvas, timing, damage, stamina, AI,

## Fighter world scale and strike reach (C-8.81C — implemented; geometry measured, device read PENDING)

- **The defect was one missing table entry.** `arena_roman.glb`'s authored visible height is **1.103**,
  and `MODEL_SCALE_CORRECTIONS` had no `roman_warrior` key — so the player *and every opponent* (every
  opponent config carries `characterModel: 'roman_warrior'`) fell through the lookup's `?? 1.0` and
  rendered at 1.103, while the four alternative bodies were normalised to the same ~1.10 rather than to
  their intended size. One number, and the reported "models render at ~60 % of intended height" and the
  short blade of C-8.81A follow from it. Full record, including every measurement table:
  [.base44/fighter-scale-c881c.md](.base44/fighter-scale-c881c.md).
- **The shipped table renders every body at its intended size** (`Fighting_Idle` t = 0.4, every skinned
  vertex through `getVertexPosition`/`localToWorld`): `roman_warrior` **1.632** (1.1035 → 1.8009),
  `amazonian` 0.990 (1.8177 → 1.7995), `dimachaerus` 0.989 (1.8208 → 1.8007), `retiarius` 0.985
  (1.8288 → 1.8014), `minotaur` **1.256** (1.7055 → 2.1421). The Minotaur keeps the shipped 1.19×
  human ratio instead of being flattened; the four humans agree on 1.800 within 2 mm.
- **`SHIELD_SCALE_GLB` 0.53 → 0.861** (= 0.55 × 1.80 / 1.15) with the 0.13 hand offset unchanged
  (0.13 × 0.861 ≈ 0.112 world units). The `SHIELD_SCALE_GLB / modelCorrection` attachment still cancels
  the body correction, so the board is **0.990** world units on all five bodies — 0.55× a human, 0.462×
  the Minotaur. At the old 0.53 it would have been 34 % of a 1.80 m body.
- **What the scale buys, measured at each clip's contact frame** (forward reach of the furthest blade
  vertex from the attacker's root; `axisGap = sep − (reach + the defender's forward extent)`, negative =
  the blade is past the opponent's silhouette; `nearest` = C-8.80E's nearest-vertex figure):

  | config | sep | clip | reach | defender | axisGap | nearest |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | shipped | 1.2 m | `Sword_Attack` | 1.2962 | 0.3615 | **−0.4577** | **0.0648** |
  | shipped | 1.2 m | `Sword_Regular_C` | 1.2931 | 0.3615 | −0.4546 | — |
  | shipped | 1.8 m | `Sword_Attack` | 1.2962 | 0.3615 | **+0.1423** | — |
  | pre-fix | 1.2 m | `Sword_Attack` | 1.0304 | 0.2215 | −0.0519 | 0.3198 |
  | pre-fix | 1.8 m | `Sword_Attack` | 1.0304 | 0.2215 | +0.5481 | — |

  So at 1.2 m the overlap grows from a marginal 0.052 to **0.458** (nearest vertex 0.32 → 0.065), and at
  **1.8 m — the first legal attack** (3.6 m opening, one 1.8 m Advance, 2.1 gladius range) — the
  shortfall drops **0.548 → 0.142**. **It is still a shortfall of 0.142**: this phase does not close
  1.8 m, and the suite pins that residual so nobody reads the scale fix as a solved contact problem.
- **Ground alignment is unchanged in kind.** The root group is never offset vertically, so the four
  bodies whose soles sit at Y = 0 still do (within 5 mm at their correction), and `arena_roman`'s own
  **0.7516** band of stray vertices below Y = 0 scales to −1.2266 (the floor hides it, as before). The
  visible height is `maxY`, never the 3.03 full bounding box — pinned separately so a future "fix"
  cannot shrink the body to make the box look right.
- **Nothing else moved:** `getWeaponRange` 2.1, damage 14/26, stamina 12/24, both 700 ms wind-ups, the
  1100 ms turn, the 1400 ms settlement, the C-8.80E attachment (still 1.000 world units of blade on every
  body), the arena, every collider, every save field and every asset byte. The production diff is two
  constant blocks in `GladiatorMesh.tsx` plus one corrected comment sentence in `weaponAttachment.ts`.
- **Suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_81c.test.ts`** — 24 tests / 85 `expect()` in ~3 s over the five real
  character GLBs and the real `gladius.glb`: §A the table parsed out of the component (keys, values, the
  default key present, no pre-fix value surviving, the 0.861 and 0.13 derivations); §B authored heights
  re-measured, every correction shown to be `target / authored`; §C rendered heights plus the pre-fix
  control (1.103 / 1.092); §D the ground; §E the shield; §F the strike table above; §G the combat

## Corrected blade-tip impact timing (C-8.81D — verified read-only pass; Android acceptance PENDING)

- **What this pass was.** A verification-and-documentation pass over the C-8.81D work that was already
  committed as `628bbfca` (branch `development-focus-strategy`). No combat rule, timer, damage, range,
  stamina, sequencing, AI or layout behaviour was changed, and no constant moved: the two contact frames
  were re-derived from the shipping assets and found correct, one documentation label was proved wrong,
  and the phase record was completed. Full record, every measurement table and the residual analysis:
  [.base44/attack-contact-c881d.md](.base44/attack-contact-c881d.md).
- **Working tree at the start and the end.** Branch `development-focus-strategy`, HEAD
  **`628bbfca429f92280b228ca2afd156df3dfe26ef`** (unchanged at the end — nothing was committed, pushed,
  merged, reset, stashed or deployed), `git status --short` **empty** at the start; the phase's earlier
  edits were already in `628bbfca`, not uncommitted. Files changed by this pass — comments and records
  only: `src/utils/attackContact.ts`, `src/utils/bladeTip.ts`, `src/utils/phaseC8_80g.test.ts`,
  `src/utils/phaseC8_81d.test.ts`, `.base44/attack-contact-c881d.md` and this section.
- **The production consumer and the exact formula.** `GladiatorMesh`'s action effect calls
  `nextAction.setEffectiveTimeScale(attackPlaybackRateForAction(activeAction, targetClip))` for every
  clip it plays; only `attack_light` / `attack_heavy` are calibrated, everything else plays at 1. The
  rate is **`contact / window`**, where `window = attackContactWindowMs()` = `PLAYER_ATTACK_WINDUP_MS −
  ATTACK_CLIP_START_LAG_MS + HIT_STOP_SAMPLE_LAG_MS` = 700 − 16.67 + 16.67 = **700 ms**, so
  `Sword_Attack` = 546/700 = **0.78** and `Sword_Regular_C` = 698/700 = **0.9971428571**. The mixer's own
  `timeScale` is *only* the hit-stop channel (`mixer.timeScale = impactAnimationScale(impactRef.current)`,
  one assignment in the frame loop), so the freeze stops the calibrated clip where it is.
- **Units, reconciled — these are three different kinds of number and the old text mixed them.**
  **546 / 698** are *milliseconds of clip time* (where each clip's blade tip is closest to the defender);
  **0.78 / 0.99714** are the *dimensionless playback rates* (`Action.setEffectiveTimeScale`, i.e.
  `contact / 700`); **0.519 / 0.828** are *world-unit tip-to-defender distances at the OLD C-8.80G frames*
  (519 / 659 ms) — the defect those frames were calibrated against, **not** the impact; **0.054** is the
  world-unit tip distance of the heavy clip at the 700 ms impact with the rate left at 1; and the light
  clip at that same rate-1 impact is **1.594** (its cut has carried through and down; the blade's nearest
  point 1.241). Nothing in the pipeline is a "normalised clip time" — the only dimensionless values are
  the two rates.
- **The documentation defect this pass found (corrected, no code change).** `attackContact.ts`'s header
  and `phaseC8_80g.test.ts`'s header both read "at the shipped 700 ms impact and rate 1 the same tip is
  0.519 / 0.828 away", which attributes the *old-frame* distances to the impact; the new suite's §C
  comment repeated the 0.519 label. All four are corrected to name the old frames for 0.519/0.828 and the
  measured rate-1 impact poses (1.594 / 0.054). `bladeTip.ts`'s tip-vertex coordinate was also stale
  (−0.006, −0.004, "within 7 mm") and now states the measured (−0.0029, −0.0020, within 3 mm). **No
  constant, formula, timer or behaviour was touched**, so this is a label repair, not a timing change.
- **The sampler contract.** `utils/bladeTip` takes the **geometry-space** vertex with the greatest Y
  (`BLADE_AXIS_LOCAL` = (0,1,0), measured from the GLB) and pushes it through `mesh.localToWorld` after
  `updateWorldMatrix(true, false)` — so one call applies the whole rendered chain: geometry → mesh node →
  the C-8.80E orientation group (+90° about X) → the `1/correction` attachment scale → the **animated
  `hand_r` bone** → the attacker's root (position, yaw, `meshScale × correction`). Re-verified this pass:
  blade point-to-pommel **0.9996** world units, pommel **0.0017** from the hand bone, and the C-8.80G
  proxy point **1.4130** from the real tip. The C-8.80G sampler mixed the gladius scene's space with the
  attachment group's, which is why its frames drifted to the tail of each swing.
- **The tests target the defender's own body, not the attacker's mesh.** The suites collect the
  *defender's* posed skinned vertices (`getVertexPosition` + `localToWorld` on
  `defender.scene`) and look the blade up **on the attachment group** (`findBladeMesh(attachment)`); the
  earlier `findBladeMesh(player.scene)` returned the fighter's own body and produced impossible 196/348 ms
  "contacts". The rebased `phaseC8_80g` / `phaseC8_81c` / `phaseC8_80j` suites keep their original
  invariants (one rate per clip, no universal multiplier, the derivation following the wind-up rather
  than a hard-coded 700, the old-frame ratio, the scale/turn/stamina/range pins) and moved only the
  values the corrected measurement changes (519 → 546, 659 → 698, the rate pair, the frame gap 140 → 152,
  "181 ms past contact" → 154 ms, and §F's re-measured strike reach) — rebased, not weakened.
- **Residual limitations, unchanged and still not solved** (all pinned in the suites, none of them a
  timing question): the heavy chop's contact is at **knee height** (nearest vertex y 0.575, torso 0.337 —
  the overhead arc passes in front of the torso and no frame in the clip touches it); the **1.2 m minimum
  gap** puts both tips *through* the body (0.2545 / 0.1578 from the nearest surface at the chosen frames;
  swept minima 0.1793 / 0.1263); the **2.1 m maximum** never reaches the body (0.2817 / 0.2426 at the
  chosen frames; swept minima 0.2808 / 0.2028); and the calibration leaves a **one-frame scheduling
  envelope** — the clip time at the held impact frame is `rate × (700 + ε − λ)` with each offset ranging
  over 0…16.67 ms, which measures 0.1939 … 0.2703 (light) and 0.2485 … 0.3805 (heavy), so the light cut
  is fixed by roughly an order of magnitude over its 1.5825 … 1.6013 rate-1 pose while the heavy is
  essentially unchanged (its contact is 2 ms before the impact). The contact basin is narrow — the tip is
  within 0.10 of the surface for only about ±5 ms around 546 — and widening it needs a clip or an
  attachment change, not a constant.

## Defense stance parity (C-8.82B — implemented, live-verified in the HUD harness)

- **Preflight (measured).** Branch `development-focus-strategy`, HEAD **`2dbebe3ded`**, `git status --short`
  **empty** at the start and no pre-existing edits; the dev stack was already up (`web` healthy on 3000).
  Nothing was reset, stashed, discarded, committed, pushed, merged or deployed. C-8.81's strike timing and
  visual diagnostics were not reopened.

- **The defect is arithmetic, not opinion.** Both stances answer the SAME mitigated blow, so through the
  shipped `calculateAttackDamage`:
  `expected guard = hit% × dmg(def, isBlocked=TRUE, blockReduction)` and
  `expected dodge = hit% × (1 − evade) × dmg(def, isBlocked=false)` — the dodge's failed roll lands
  UNMITIGATED. The hit% cancels, so the verdict is `(1 − evade)` against `(1 − blockReduction)`. At 0.75 the
  roster's shields (gladius 0.82, shamshir 0.80, spatha 0.85) passed less through than a dodge avoided **and**
  recovered stamina on a stopped blow, so over `ALL_WEAPONS` × the opponent weapon set (11 × 4 × 2 attacks =
  **88 configurations**) **30** had `dodge ≥ guard` on damage while the guard was also the only one that could
  gain stamina. Documented defender (C-8.72B's shield build): `defense 42`, `agility 16`, `staminaRegen 31.9`;
  attacker `strength 12`, `agility 14` (58 % heavy / 82 % quick).
- **The sweep, before choosing.** The block-reduction lever was measured and rejected: `blockReduction` is
  per-weapon data used by whoever blocks, so lowering it to below an evade rate would weaken the shields of
  the player AND of every shield-wielding opponent (Marcus, Drusus) and gut the archetype — a much broader
  shift than the stance it was meant to fix. The evade rate is the one lever that moves only Dodge.
  | rate | configs where dodge ≥ guard | worst dodge gain over guard |
  |---|---|---|
  | 0.75 (shipped) | **30 / 88** | **−66.7 %** (spatha guard vs gladius heavy) |
  | 0.86 | 0 / 88 | +6.7 % |
  | 0.87 | 0 / 88 | +13.3 % |
  | **0.88 (chosen)** | **0 / 88** | **+20.0 %** |
  **0.86 is the first rate that merely breaks the dominance; 0.88 is the smallest whole-percent rate at which
  the roster's heaviest attack is cut by a meaningful ≥ 15 % against EVERY weapon's guard**, so the choice is
  the criterion, not taste. Light weapons do not reverse the trade-off, they gain more: the worst light build
  (`dual_vipers` 0.48 vs the hoplite's quick thrust) gains **76.0 %**, the best shield entry
  (`titan_colossus_mace` 0.75 vs the gladius' quick thrust) **56.0 %**.
- **The heaviest attack, before → after** (`dmg 72` = `titan_colossus_mace`, defender `spatha` 0.85 —
  the least favourable pair; the opponent set's own heaviest is `bronze_mace` 42, whose worst pair is
  spatha at **20.8 %**):
  | | guard | dodge |
  |---|---|---|
  | 0.75 | **8** | 14.0 — **75 % WORSE than guarding** |
  | 0.88 | **8** | **6.72 — 16.0 % better** |
  Against the standard gladius shield (guard 10) the same dodge pays 14.0 → 6.72, i.e. −75 % → **+32.8 %**.
- **Whose balance moved — both, symmetrically and measurably, and the effect was quantified, not waved away.**
  The rate is shared by the player's and the AI's `dodge` stance (one roll, one constant), so an opponent that
  dodges evades the player's strike 88 % of the time instead of 75. AI *selection* weights are untouched, so
  the effect is the payoff only: measured over `ALL_OPPONENTS` the mean P(AI picks dodge) is **16.3 %**
  (max 37.3 %, Marcus), and the player's expected damage into a dodging opponent falls from 25 % to 12 % of
  the unblocked figure — **−2.4 % overall, −6.7 % in the worst fight (Marcus)**. No enemy damage, hit chance,
  crit, reward or aggression value moved.
- **One source of truth.** `DODGE_EVADE_CHANCE = 0.88` and its derived `DODGE_EVADE_PERCENT = 88`
  (`combatCalculations.ts`, beside `DODGE_STAMINA_COST`); `DuelScene`'s roll now reads the constant (no
  literal anywhere), and `TurnActionPanel`, `HelpModal`, `CombatHUD` and `pendingStrike.resolveReactionCue`
  all derive their copy from it. The reaction cue gained the trade-off: the pre-decision row now reads
  "Shield Guard · {block}% cut · no cost" and "Dodge −12 SP · {88}% evade" (both live in the shipped HUD —
  verified below), and the claimed line reads
  "Dodge set — 88 % chance to slip the blow entirely; 12 SP spent." / "Guard set — the blow lands at reduced
  force (82 % absorbed by the shield)." No hardcoded evade percentage remains in the UI or the manual.
- **Files changed — five production, three rebased suites, one new suite, this record.**
  `src/utils/combatCalculations.ts` (the constant, the derived percent, the doc comments);
  `src/components/duel/DuelScene.tsx` (import + the roll + its comment);
  `src/components/ui/TurnActionPanel.tsx`; `src/components/hub/HelpModal.tsx`;
  `src/components/ui/CombatHUD.tsx` (the row's odds, and the cue receiving the fighter's block reduction);
  `src/utils/pendingStrike.ts` (the cue's labels and its optional `blockReduction` argument);
  **Rebased, not weakened:** `defensiveBalance.test.ts` (§C's "unchanged 75 %" pin now pins the CONSTANT and
  forbids a literal — the literal it used to assert is now the thing it rejects; the manual pin reads
  `{DODGE_EVADE_PERCENT}` and rejects any `N% chance to evade`), `phaseC8_79C.test.ts` (the rate it reads out
  of the resolution now resolves a constant NAME as well as a literal, and the pin asserts it equals
  `DODGE_EVADE_CHANCE` — 2 further assertions), `phaseC8_79B.test.ts` (the HUD still resolves the cue from the
  `reactionTaken` prop; the pin tolerates the new second argument). **New:** `src/utils/phaseC8_82b.test.ts`.
- **Regression suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_82b.test.ts` — 27 tests / 267 `expect()`.** §A one source of truth
  (the constant and its derived percent; the roll; the panel, manual, HUD row and cue all derive; no hardcoded

  the structural `1 − evade < 1 − bestBlock` rule; **0 of 88** dominated after vs **30 of 88** before, with the
  −66.67 % worst case replayed as a control; light weapons gaining more, not less); §C the meaningful benefit

- **Verified 2026-10-19** in the dev container: focused `phaseC8_82b + defensiveBalance +

## Failed-dodge feedback (C-8.82D — implemented)

- **The gap C-8.82B created.** With Dodge at parity (0.88 evade), a dodge that was RAISED and then
  BEATEN resolved as an unblocked hit, and the chronicle wrote the same line an open guard produces:
  `X struck Y for N damage.` The player had just paid the 12 SP, the stance was spent, damage went
  through — and nothing in the log said the dodge was taken and failed. Read as "the dodge did
  nothing", at exactly the point the balance work landed.

- **The correction is one pure copy module plus its call site.** `src/utils/strikeFeedback.ts` owns
  the landed-strike wording: `DODGE_FAILED_MARKER` (`'DODGE FAILS'`, one literal) and
  `landedStrikeText({ attackerName, defenderName, damage, isCrit, dodgeFailed = false })`.
  `DuelScene`'s unblocked-hit branch builds the line once and passes it to the **same** `addLog` call
  the blow already made (`'crit'` for a critical, `player`/`opponent` otherwise), so one incoming
  attack can never log twice, report two damage figures or contradict itself. `dodgeFailed` defaults
  to false, so open-guard, blocked and evaded wording is byte-identical to before; the failed-dodge
  line names the defender, keeps the real damage figure and still leads with `CRITICAL BLOW!` on a
  crit. Nothing here touches stamina, damage, timing or RNG.

- **`defender.isInvulnerable` is the truthful source for the flag, and that is why it is used.** A
  dodge sets it and the stance survives the turn boundary; the blocked path is its own `isBlocked`
  branch with its own BLOCKED line; the passive-evade path (counter_dodge bosses) explicitly excludes
  `isInvulnerable`, so inside the unblocked hit branch a true value can only mean an active dodge
  whose evade roll failed.

- **Regression suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_82d.test.ts`** — 18 tests / 76 `expect()` across 5 sections:
  §A the one shared marker (present exactly once on a failed dodge, absent from an open-guard hit,
  a single literal in the module); §B the copy states what happened (one damage figure, one sentence,
  no `MISS` / `EVADED` / `BLOCKED` / "no damage" claim, differs from the open-guard line for the same
  hit); §C crits stay legible and non-crits are not dressed up; §D the default path is untouched
  (omitted argument, explicit `false` and the open-guard crit line are exact strings); §E production
  wiring (the helper imported, `dodgeFailed: defender.isInvulnerable`, exactly two `addLog(strikeLine,`
  sites, no DuelScene-level copy of the marker, the BLOCKED line intact). The "module never logs"
  check reads the source **with comments stripped** — the module's own docstring names its callers'
  `addLog`, which is a comment, not behaviour.

- **One existing suite was rebased, not weakened.** `phaseC8_75F.test.ts` executes the real
  `executeCombatTurn` body extracted from `DuelScene.tsx` against a harness of live production
  bindings; the new call made it throw `ReferenceError: landedStrikeText is not defined` and took 6
  of its 14 tests with it (its own design: a missing binding fails loudly instead of passing
  vacuously). `landedStrikeText` is now imported and bound alongside `calculateAttackDamage`,
  `canResolveStrikeImpact` and the rest, with a comment naming this phase. No expectation changed.

- **Verified 2026-10-25** in the dev container: focused `phaseC8_82d + phaseC8_82b +
  defensiveBalance + pendingStrike + combatActionOrder + combatResponsiveness` → **135 pass / 0 fail**;
  `bun test` → **3771 pass / 0 fail, 93791 `expect()` across 134 files** (the branch tip's baseline
  was 3753 / 135 files with the 6 `phaseC8_75F` failures this turn fixed — the delta is this suite's
  18 tests); `bun run scripts/combatTests.ts` → **69 passed, 0 failed**; `bun run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`)
