## Idempotent Dodge reaction cost (C-8.83B — implemented)

- **The defect was one stance charged twice.** A player who set Dodge on their OWN turn
  kept the stance across the turn boundary (`resolveTurnEndDefensive` preserves it, by design),
  so when the enemy's strike was announced the stance was already standing — and selecting
  Dodge again in the reaction window ran `reactToPendingAttack`'s unconditional debit, charging
  another 12 SP and incrementing `dodgesPerformed` a second time for the same stance.

- **The correction is ONE pure rule plus its call site.** `planDodgeReaction(stance, stamina)`
  in `src/utils/combatCalculations.ts` (beside the stance helpers) answers the reaction's charge
  as `{ kind: 'activate' | 'reaffirm' | 'refused', staminaCost, countsDodge }`:
  `activate` = 12 SP and one dodge counted; `reaffirm` (the stance is already held) = **0 SP and
  no count**, the stance simply staying up for the pending blow; `refused` = an unaffordable NEW
  stance. `DuelScene`'s `reactToPendingAttack` now reads it from `fightersRef.current.player` —
  **the same snapshot the impact resolves against** — refuses a `refused` plan BEFORE
  `claimReaction()` (so an unaffordable dodge still does not burn the announcement's one
  reaction), then debits `dodgeCharge.staminaCost` once and increments the counter only when
  `countsDodge`. A reaffirm still claims the reaction, still writes the stance through
  `applyDefensiveAction(clearDefensiveStance(prev), 'dodge')`, still names the dodge in the
  chronicle and still shows `DODGE!` — nothing about the answer is lost, only the second charge.

- **Why a free reaffirm cannot arm an unrelated strike.** The stance is consumed by
  `clearDefensiveStance` at the top of the fighter's next `executeCombatTurn`, and the turn order
  puts that action before any later announcement, so an active dodge stance at reaction time IS
  the stance for this pending strike. One claim per announcement (`claimReaction`) means the free
  path runs at most once, and the turn-action `dodge` branch still debits every time it is taken
  (both fighters, twice in the branch). The ordinary activation is 12 SP with the unchanged
  refusal at `< DODGE_STAMINA_COST` — a stance already held needs no stamina, which is the one
  behavioural consequence: a player at 0 SP can still confirm the dodge they already paid for.

- **Nothing else moved.** No change to `DODGE_STAMINA_COST` (12), `DODGE_EVADE_CHANCE` (0.88),
  `ENEMY_ATTACK_WINDUP_MS` / `PLAYER_ATTACK_WINDUP_MS` (700), the impact's
  `defender.isInvulnerable && Math.random() < DODGE_EVADE_CHANCE` roll, Shield Guard (still free,
  still writes no stamina), the passive evade, the miss path, the 1100 ms resolution or the
  C-8.82D failed-dodge wording. The AI Dodge affordability clamp is deliberately **not** touched.

- **Truthful feedback (the cue and the control).** The reaction cue used to say "12 SP spent" for
  every dodge; `resolveReactionCue(reaction, blockReduction, dodgeStaminaSpent = true)` now takes
  a third argument and a reaffirm reads *"Dodge held — 88% chance to slip the blow entirely; the
  stance was already paid for."* `DuelScene` tracks the one boolean (`reactionDodgeCharged`,
  reset with `reactionTaken`) and the HUD passes it through; the default keeps every existing
  caller byte-identical. The HUD's dodge reaction control is gated on
  `player.stamina < DODGE_STAMINA_COST && !player.isInvulnerable` and labels a held stance
  `Dodge · held` / `88% evade · no cost`, so the button can neither advertise a charge it will
  not make nor refuse an answer that costs nothing.

- **Regression suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_83B.test.ts`** — 28 tests / 321 `expect()` across six
  sections: §A the rule (first activation 12 SP once, reaffirm 0 and uncounted, reaffirm free at
  0 SP, refusal below the cost with the exact boundary, a guard stance still paying, purity and a
  0…100 sweep); §B the lifecycle (turn-end preservation, the pre-clear that makes a later strike a
  fresh activation, five reaffirms accumulating nothing, the turn-action branch still charging
  twice); §C the impact (the shipped roll line, the 88 % boundary at 0.8799 / 0.88, the untouched
  timings); §D the wiring (plan from the impact snapshot, refusal before claim, claim before every
  stance write, one debit of `dodgeCharge.staminaCost`, one `dodgesPerformed += 1` behind
  `countsDodge`, the cue flag); §E nothing else moved (guard, blocked branch, passive evade, miss,
  failed-dodge copy, constants); §F the cue and the control, **rendered** with
  `renderToStaticMarkup` (a held stance at 0 SP is enabled and reads `Dodge · held`, an open one
  is disabled and reads `Dodge −12 SP`, and a reaffirm cue claims no charge).

- **Five source-pinned assertions were rebased, not weakened — each moved to the new single
  source, none removed.** `defensiveBalance` §C and `combatResponsiveness` §C (the reaction's one
  debit: `prev.stamina - DODGE_STAMINA_COST` → `prev.stamina - dodgeCharge.staminaCost`, plus
  `planDodgeReaction(` present and the literal gone), `phaseC8_79B` §B/§D (the HUD's gate now
  carries `&& !player.isInvulnerable`; the cue call is the three-argument form), `phaseC8_79C` §D
  (the refusal order pin moved to `dodgeCharge.kind === 'refused'`, still before the claim), and
  `phaseC8_74D` §D (the 44px window now runs to the target's own `</button>` — strictly stronger
  than the fixed 400 characters, because the dodge control gained a two-line comment).
  `phaseC8_75F`'s harness executes the real `reactToPendingAttack` body, so it now binds
  `planDodgeReaction` and `setReactionDodgeCharged` alongside the other shipped helpers — its own
  design (a missing binding fails loudly rather than passing vacuously) is what caught it.

- **Verified 2026-10-25** in the dev container: focused
  `bun test` over the 14 defensive/reaction suites → **327 pass / 0 fail (2 325 `expect()`)**;
  `bun test` → **3799 pass / 0 fail (135 files, 94 120 `expect()`)** (the branch tip read 3771 /
  134; the delta is this suite's 28 tests and its file); `bun run scripts/combatTests.ts` →
  **69 passed, 0 failed**; `bun run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) → exit 0; `bun run build` → exit 0 with
  the startup-asset check passing (8 assets); `git diff --check` → clean. The validation's
  starting point was **6 failing assertions** (four rebases plus `phaseC8_75F`'s unbound helper and
  one `tsc` error in the new suite), all fixed in the tests or the harness, none by loosening a
  check.

- **Browser evidence (preview, anonymous visitor — no session replayed), and its limits.** The
  shipped `CombatHUD` was driven in the repo's own `?devHarness=hud&hudState=power` harness, loaded
  inside an in-page frame (the C-8.66C/C-8.68C technique, because the preview host rewrites a
  top-level query string): the dodge control rendered `Dodge −12 SP · 88% evade` and enabled, a
  real click claimed the reaction (`data-hud-reacts="dodge"`), both controls were replaced, and the
  cue read **"Dodge set — 88% chance to slip the blow entirely; 12 SP spent."** — i.e. the
  ordinary, charged path still reports its charge through the new three-argument call — with the
  frame removed afterwards and no console errors. **The reaffirm state itself was NOT driven in
  the browser:** the harness's fighter fixture is `isInvulnerable: false` and there is no control
  to set it, so that path is verified by the suite's rendered `renderToStaticMarkup` assertions
  (`Dodge · held`, `no cost`, the "already paid for" cue) rather than in a live duel.
  **Not automatically verified: the live duel itself** — one stance charged once needs a real
  announcement answered after a real turn-action dodge, and the arena renders at ~2 fps through

## Turn-action Dodge affordability (Phase C-8.84A — implemented)

- **The defect was real and confirmed in source, one step short of a live one.** The player's
  turn-action Dodge had no affordability guard: `executeCombatTurn`'s dodge branch billed with
  `Math.max(0, prev.stamina - DODGE_STAMINA_COST)` (twice — once per fighter), which CLAMPS rather
  than refuses. Invoked at 0-11 SP it set `isInvulnerable`, incremented
  `statsRef.current.dodgesPerformed` and consumed the turn for a partial or zero charge. It was not
  reachable by an ordinary tap — `TurnActionPanel` already disables the Dodge button below 12 SP —
  so the hole was the same class C-8.75E closed for strikes: a stale panel, or any direct call to
  `executeCombatTurn('player', 'dodge')`, could still buy a stance it had not paid for.
- **The fix is one predicate and one guard.** `canAffordDodge(stamina)` sits beside
  `planDodgeReaction` in `combatCalculations.ts` (same 12 SP threshold, non-finite stamina reads as
  unaffordable exactly like `canAffordAttack`). `executeCombatTurn` now refuses a player Dodge the
  same way it refuses an unaffordable strike — after the range and strike-affordability guards,
  **before `resolvingRef.current = true`, before the stance pre-clear and before the counter** — and
  logs `${name} is too winded to take an evasion stance.` to the existing `'system'` channel. A
  refused Dodge therefore leaves the turn, a held stance and `dodgesPerformed` untouched.
- **Deliberately unchanged.** The branch keeps its clamp (C-8.75E left the strike branch the same
  way; the guard upstream is what makes it unreachable below the cost). `planDodgeReaction` keeps
  its own `stamina < DODGE_STAMINA_COST` test, so the C-8.83B reaction path and its free
  reaffirmation are untouched — including reaffirming a held stance at 0 SP. **The opponent's Dodge
  is NOT guarded in this phase** (`chooseAITacticalAction` still offers it with no stamina test), so
  the pre-existing ROSTER asymmetry — the AI can buy the 88 % evade for less than 12 SP — remains
  open and is the next audit in this workstream.
  **Phase C-8.84B closed it — see its section at the end of this file.**
- **Suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_84A.test.ts`** (23 tests / 159 `expect()`) — section A the guard's
  placement (player-only, after the strike guards, before the commit, the pre-clear and the counter)
  and the branch's kept clamp; B the 0-11 / 12 / above threshold plus the non-finite case; C the turn
  action end to end at every stamina including the negative control that reproduces the pre-fix free
  stance; D the reaction path and the zero-cost reaffirmation; E Shield Guard, strike affordability
  and both refusal copies. The driver uses the real helpers and section A binds its write order to
  the shipped handler.
- **Verified 2026-10-26** in the dev container: focused
  `bun test` over C-8.83B, C-8.83D, `defensiveBalance`, `combatActionOrder`, `combatResponsiveness`,

## AI turn-action Dodge affordability (Phase C-8.84B — implemented)

- **The defect, reproduced in the shipped helper before anything was edited.** The opponent's
  in-range chain only ever compared stamina to the LIGHT attack's cost (`context.stamina < lightCost`
  selects the low-stamina branch), so a weapon whose light strike costs less than a Dodge let the
  opponent reach the `chooseAIStandardAction` pool with too little stamina for the stance, and that
  pool can return `dodge`. Resolution then billed it with
  `Math.max(0, prev.stamina - DODGE_STAMINA_COST)` — a CLAMP, which refuses nothing — and the C-8.84A
  turn guard was narrowed to `isActorPlayer`. Measured against the shipped roster (opponents resolve
  their weapon through `getWeaponByType`): `dual_blades` resolves to `dual_sicae_daggers`
  (light **9**) and `spear` to `hoplite_spear` (light **11**), so **Flaccus and Ignis could draw
  Dodge at 9, 10 and 11 SP, and Cassius and Valéria at 11 SP**, each receiving the stance, its 88 %
  evade and a dodge for a cost they had not paid.
- **The fix is one rule in each half of the C-8.75E contract, and nothing else moved.**
  - SELECTION — `enforceAffordableAIAction` now answers for `dodge` too, through the C-8.84A
    predicate: `canAffordDodge(stamina) ? 'dodge' : 'shield_block'`. It runs before the strike
    rules, so every branch that can name a Dodge passes through it, and it draws no randomness, so
    the probability stream cannot shift.
  - RESOLUTION — the C-8.84A guard lost its `isActorPlayer` narrowing, so the opponent's Dodge is
    refused at the commit boundary as well, and an opponent's refusal now hands the turn back
    (`setIsExecuting(false); setIsPlayerTurn(true)`) exactly as the range and strike refusals do —
    without it a refused AI action would leave the HUD locked with no turn to take.
  - FALLBACK — an unaffordable Dodge becomes `shield_block`, not `rest`: the guard costs nothing, is
    already an outcome of the shipped low-stamina branch (so no new kind of turn exists), keeps the
    turn defensive, and mints no stamina the way `rest`'s +40 would. Nothing else changed — cost 12,
    88 % evade, stance lifetime, Shield Guard, strike costs, weapon balance, opponent stats and
    every timing constant are untouched, and the reaction path's free reaffirmation is not involved.
- **Rebased, not weakened: four sites pinned the old contract.** `phaseC8_75E`'s "non-strike actions
  are never rewritten" list contained `dodge` — the defect itself; it now names the three free
  actions and pins Dodge as enforced below/at its cost. `phaseC8_84A`'s "the guard is player-only"
  test now asserts the guard is NOT actor-narrowed and that the AI module reads `canAffordDodge`.
  `combatActionOrder`, `playerStrikeWindup` and `playerWindupCue` each pin the count of
  `setIsPlayerTurn(` sites; the Dodge refusal's release makes it 4, and `combatActionOrder`
  additionally shows that fourth one sits inside the Dodge guard, before its return.
- **Suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_84B.test.ts`** (34 tests / 74 357 `expect()`) — A the roster band
  measured plus a pre-fix control that still selects Dodge there; B no branch and no draw selects
  Dodge at 0-11 SP (all four weapon types × both blocking states × both health states × 201 draws)
  including the 9/10/11 and 11 SP roster edges, every catalogue weapon and non-finite stamina;
  C Dodge still reachable at the cost and above; D the fallback is legal, free and mints nothing
  (the Shield Guard branch is asserted to contain no `stamina` write at all); E the shipped chain
  equals a pre-fix replica wherever the Dodge is affordable, plus the unchanged pool thresholds;
  F both boundaries bound to the shipped source by order; G the player's C-8.84A contract; H the
  reaction planner and its zero-cost reaffirmation.
- **Verified 2026-10-26** in the dev container (branch `development-focus-strategy`, base HEAD
  `26c8ee892b`, tree clean at start): covering suites
  (`grep -rln` over `aiActionSelection` / `DuelScene.tsx` → 35 files) → **856 pass / 0 fail**;
  `bun run scripts/combatTests.ts` → **69 passed, 0 failed**; `bun run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) →
  exit 0; `bun run build` → exit 0 with the startup-asset check passing (8 assets); `git diff

## Dodge UI and feedback consistency (Phase C-8.84D — implemented)

- **Two defects confirmed in source before anything was edited; both were real, neither was already
  fixed.** (1) The player's two Dodge controls compared stamina directly —
  `CombatHUD`'s reaction button `player.stamina < DODGE_STAMINA_COST && !player.isInvulnerable` and
  `TurnActionPanel`'s Dodge card `player.stamina < DODGE_STAMINA_COST` — while C-8.84A/B's engine
  guard answers to `canAffordDodge`. The two agree for every finite stamina ≥ 0, which is why the
  divergence was invisible, and disagree exactly where the predicate was written for: `NaN`,
  `+Infinity` and a non-numeric `stamina` all compare FALSE against 12, so both controls offered a
  stance the engine then refuses. (`-Infinity` compares low, so it was already gated.) (2) The shared
  `shield_block` branch logged `"<name> braces behind their shield."` and cued `BRACED!` for every
  loadout, so the shield-less fighters C-8.84B's fallback sends there (the roster's `dual_blades`

  `CombatHUD` derives `reactionDodgeBlocked = !canAffordDodge(player.stamina) && !player.isInvulnerable`
  (the `isInvulnerable` operand is what keeps C-8.83B's free reaffirmation alive, including at 0 SP and
  at a non-finite stamina — `planDodgeReaction` charges a held stance nothing), and

## Dodge vs Shield Guard balance audit (Phase C-8.85A — read-only, no production change)

- **Preflight, as measured (differs from the requested baseline, and preserved rather than restored).**
  Branch `development-focus-strategy`, HEAD **`befccc30b56d31b782277b35d31165e2fe657258`**, `git status
  --short` **empty** before and after. The brief expected HEAD `6a35b904` with the C-8.84F work
  uncommitted; in fact C-8.84F is **`befccc3` "Implement shield-feedback logic for dual guard states"**,
  whose parent is exactly `6a35b904`. The change set is intact — nothing was reset, stashed, discarded,
  rebased, committed, pushed, merged or deployed, and **no production file was edited**.

- **Verdict: Shield Guard dominates Dodge over realistic bouts, and the cause is the resource rule, not
  the evade rate.** The C-8.82B pass fixed the *damage* axis correctly and its conclusion still holds
  (Dodge's per-strike mitigation beats a shield's block). What it could not see — because it compared a
  single hit with `hit%` cancelled — is that **Guard is free and profitable while Dodge costs a fixed
  12 SP per announcement against a pool that pays for 11**. Evidence below is a deterministic model
  driving the shipped `calculateAttackDamage`, `calculateHitChance`, `shieldGuardStaminaGain`,
  `canAffordDodge`, `chooseAITacticalAction` and `calculateTotalStats` (throwaway scripts, container
  `/tmp` only: `c885a-audit.ts`, `c885a-model2.ts`, `c885a-cand.ts`).

- **Path A — the reaction window (the dominant path).** `CombatHUD`'s Shield Guard reaction button
  carries **no `disabled` at all** (the Dodge button carries `reactionDodgeBlocked`), so it can be
  raised at **0 SP, every announcement, without spending the turn action**. It writes
  `isBlocking`, and the shared impact branch then credits `shieldGuardStaminaGain` on the stopped
  blow. Dodge pays 12 SP from the same window (`planDodgeReaction`), refunds nothing, and is refused
  below 12. So on the player's side the two answers are **free-and-profitable vs 12-SP-and-capped**.
- **Path B — the turn action.** Guard costs 0 and credits nothing on the raise; Dodge costs 12.
  Guard additionally feeds the AI's branch 1 (`playerIsBlocking`): measured over a 2000-point sweep of
  the shipped `chooseAITacticalAction`, holding a guard drops P(attack) from **85 / 90 / 95 %** to
  **45 %** for Ignis / Valéria / Aurelius (unchanged 45 % for Cassius). The turn-action **Dodge is
  strictly dominated by the reaction Dodge** — same 12 SP price, but it can be wasted whenever the
  enemy taunts or braces instead of striking, because the stance is consumed by the player's own next
  action. The turn-action Guard is *not* dominated by the reaction Guard, because only it bends the
  AI's branch.

- **The arithmetic, measured.** Shield kit (gladius 0.82, def 51, agi 18, hp 321, pool 140, regen
  34.6, all through `calculateTotalStats`) against the whole roster, per announced strike:
  guard **1.4–6.5 HP and +8.0…+13.6 SP**; dodge **0.8–4.3 HP and −12 SP**. Over the C-8.82B
  configuration sweep, Dodge's *expected damage* is lower in **63/64** shield-tier pairs and **96/96**
  shield-less pairs — the one exception is a `Math.max(1, …)` floor artefact (Marcus quick vs spatha:
  guard 0.73 vs dodge 0.88). Yet HP saved per announcement is **0.42–2.21** for a **20–23 SP swing**,
  which is **1.9–2.1 light gladius strikes ≈ 43–53 enemy HP forgone** — one to two orders of magnitude
  the wrong way. Worst case also favours Guard: Aurelius heavy vs spatha, guard 8 (**12** on a crit)
  against dodge's **55** (**83** on a crit) when the 12 % fails.
- **Capacity is the ceiling no evade rate can lift.** `staminaMax / DODGE_STAMINA_COST` allows **11**
  paid answers (10 for the skirmish kit, 10 for a starter), while the roster's later bouts present
  **~12–33** announcements. Past eleven, Dodge is simply refused and the fighter eats the blow
  unmitigated, while Guard is still free and still crediting.

- **Bout projection (EV model, player attacks light every turn and answers every announcement).**
  Shipped behaviour, HP remaining out of 321: Dodge wins only the two shortest bouts by **+2 HP**
  (Marcus 319 v 317, Flaccus 316 v 314), ties Cassius (314 v 314), and loses everywhere longer —
  Goliath 301 v 305, Ignis 284 v 294, Drusus 275 v 299, Valéria 227 v 271, **Aurelius 90 v 183**. Dodging
  also starves the offence: the Aurelius bout stretches from **30 to 48 rounds**, so the defence that
  saves 1.7 HP per announcement costs two-and-a-half strikes of stamina and lengthens the fight that
  generates the attacks. The one place Dodge is meaningfully better is the **shield-less** build
  (0.35–0.52 block), where it saves 3.6–14.1 HP per announcement — the archetype split C-8.72B
  intended, and it survives intact.

- **Recommendation (finding 3, minimal adjustment justified — NOT implemented).** The smallest lever
  that needs no tuned value changed is to **settle the reaction Dodge's 12 SP at impact, against the
  blow it had to evade, instead of unconditionally at the announcement** — the mirror of the rule the
  guard already follows (`shieldGuardStaminaGain` pays only when a blow is actually stopped). Only the
  `activate` kind is affected (`planDodgeReaction`'s free `reaffirm` stays free), and the price, the
  88 % rate, `blockReduction`, the guard's credit, the damage formula and every AI weight are
  untouched. Measured in the same model this cuts Dodge's expected price to `12 × hit%` (**7.4–9.4 SP**
  rather than 12), lifts its capacity from 11 to ~17 announcements, flips Goliath and Drusus to
  Dodge and narrows the Aurelius HP gap from **93 to 28**. **It narrows, it does not reverse**: closing
  the remainder needs the price-side lever this phase forbids touching, so a follow-up phase is where
  that decision belongs. Withdrawing the reaction guard's stamina credit (candidate C1) was modelled
  and **rejected** — it hurts Guard more than Dodge (Aurelius 156 v 90) and leaves the dominance
  intact. Regression risks for the proposed change: the debit moves out of `reactToPendingAttack` into
  the impact branch, so `defensiveBalance` §C's "debits it once, before any roll" pin and the HUD's
  "12 SP spent" cue both need rebasing; `dodgesPerformed` must still count once; affordability must
  still be settled at the claim (nothing else can spend inside the locked window).

- **Verified / not verified.** Focused `bun test` over `phaseC8_82b`, `defensiveBalance`, `phaseC8_83B`,
  `phaseC8_84A`, `phaseC8_84B`, `phaseC8_84D`, `phaseC8_84F`, `combatResponsiveness`, `phaseC8_75E` →
  **267 pass / 0 fail** (9 files, 76642 `expect()`). The full suite was **not** run (read-only audit).
  No production value, test or source file changed, so no behaviour moved. Every combat number here is
  from **unit-level production helpers plus a deterministic EV model** — **not** from a live duel, and
  the model assumes a steady-state AI stance mix, light attacks every turn, no potions and a single
  attacker; it is a comparative instrument, not a forecast of a specific bout. **No live-duel or
  Android acceptance is claimed.**

## Reaction Dodge cost contract (Phase C-8.85B — read-only design gate, no production change)

- **Preflight (differs from the brief; preserved, not restored).** Branch `development-focus-strategy`,
  HEAD **`af0f7089ef531e869b053a2bbb2ab14d73e10e50`** "Audit shield guard and dodge balance",
  `git status --porcelain` **empty** before and after. The brief expected HEAD `befccc30b5` with the
  C-8.85A record still *uncommitted*; it is in fact **committed** as `af0f708`, one commit on top of
  `befccc3` (C-8.84F, its parent), and its 83 lines are intact above. Nothing was reset, stashed,
  amended, committed, pushed, merged or deployed, and **no production file was edited**.

- **The contract is already written down (C-8.83B), so it is read, not inferred.** `planDodgeReaction`
  (`utils/combatCalculations.ts`): `DODGE_STAMINA_COST` "buys the dodge STANCE, not the tap" —
  `activate` = 12 SP + `dodgesPerformed += 1`; `reaffirm` (stance already held) = 0 SP and no second
  dodge; `refused` (stamina < 12) = 0 SP. `reactToPendingAttack` (`DuelScene.tsx` L1298) charges
  through it at the CLAIM: after the refusal test, before `claimReaction()` spends the announcement's
  one reaction, and before any dice.

- **Which paths can raise a reaction stance at all.** The window exists only inside
  `announceEnemyAttack`, which has exactly two call sites — the standard strike (L1497, reached only
  when `dist <= weapon.range`) and Valéria's queued counter (L1444). Taunt, brace/`shield_block`,
  advance, retreat, rest and `telegraph` all resolve through `executeCombatTurn` directly (L1501) and
  never announce, so a reaction Dodge is not offered and **nothing can be charged for them**. There is
  no feint, cancelled or interrupted wind-up in the codebase.

- **On the reaction path the 12 SP is never wasted — in the shipped roster.** `announceEnemyAttack` sets
  `isExecuting`, and every `TurnActionPanel` control is gated on it (L196-401), so distance is frozen
  for the window; `strikeRef.announce` refuses a second announce; `cancel()` is only reachable from the
  confirmed withdrawal, the match-end effect and unmount, all of which need the bout already over. So
  the landing always runs and the stance always meets a resolving strike. The one *latent* lost-charge
  path is the counter's own: it is announced with **no range check** while its landing re-runs the
  authoritative range guard, and it is **unreachable today** only because every player weapon's range
  (max 3.3, spear) is <= Valéria's spear reach, so any distance at which the player's strike was legal
  is inside hers. That is an announce-side bug to fix if a shorter-range `counter_dodge` opponent is
  ever added — not a cost-contract question.

- **Where a charge IS lost is the turn action, and it is lost two ways.** A turn-action Dodge stance
  dies at the top of the fighter's next action (pre-clear, L684-699), so it buys nothing whenever the
  enemy's turn is a non-strike (`1 − aggression`, i.e. 5-50 % by opponent). It is also wasted against
  Goliath's telegraphed heavy: that blow resolves **directly** (L1414) with no announcement, so there
  is no reaction row at all, and if the player's stance turn was a retreat the mace's reach is left and
  the guard refuses the heavy — 12 SP spent where a free retreat would have done the same job.

- **A reaction Dodge also REPLACES a held guard.** Both reaction branches run
  `applyDefensiveAction(clearDefensiveStance(prev), …)` (L1330 / L1345), so dodging an announced strike
  while holding a free 82 % guard pays 12 SP *and* gives up the guard and its 17.3 SP credit. That is
  the dominance problem in its sharpest form, and it is a cue/copy question rather than a price one.

- **Policies priced per announcement (production helpers, roster of 8, C-8.85A kit).** **A** current
  12.0 · **B** impact-settled **12.0 — the same number**, because the announcement already guarantees an
  impact, so B differs only on the withdrawal/unmount paths where the bout is over · **B′** (charge only
  if the blow *would* have landed) 7.7, against the roster's mean P(land) 64.4 % — **that is the
  C-8.85A "7.4–9.4 SP" figure, and it belongs to B′, a policy the list does not contain**: the impact
  reads the stance *before* the hit roll (L936), so "resolves against the active Dodge" cannot depend on
  `hitPct` · **C** (successful evade) 10.56, i.e. −12 %, and it makes a FAILED dodge free — the worst
  outcome pays nothing, and the price stops being knowable at the HUD · **D** capacity only: 11 dodges
  today, 14 at 10 SP, 17 at 8, 23 at 6.

- **Model challenged and reproduced.** `calculateAttackDamage` / `calculateHitChance` /
  `shieldGuardStaminaGain` (17.3 SP credit per stopped blow, `×0.5`, clamped at `staminaMax`) give a
  shield kit **1.5–5.5 HP per announcement** under Guard and **0.9–3.6** under Dodge — the audit's
  magnitudes, and shield-less Dodge saves **3.7–14.6 HP**. Reproducing the capacity ceiling explains
  the audit's table: after N = 11 announcements Dodge is ahead (162 vs 245 HP lost across the roster),
  at N = 12 it is already behind (286 vs 267), at N = 20 it is catastrophic (1270 vs 445) because every
  dodge past the pool is refused and the blow lands unmitigated. **Dodge's edge is an artefact of short
  bouts; the 12 SP is exhausted before the roster's later fights pay out.**

- **Why no price in the A–E list fixes it — measured in the game's own currency.** Guard already absorbs
  82 % of a blow for 0 SP, so Dodge's *unique* avoidance is **6 % of a blow** for a shield build and
  **48 %** shield-less (blockRed 0.40). Priced by the guard's own credit yardstick (17.3 SP per 82 %
  stopped ≈ 0.21 SP per 1 % of a blow) that marginal avoidance is worth **≈1.3 SP** to a shield fighter
  and **≈20.8 SP** to a shield-less one. One flat price cannot serve a ~15× spread, so **D is rejected on
  evidence rather than taste**; B moves nothing and C moves 12 %. The yardstick is an inference from
  `SHIELD_GUARD_REGEN_MULTIPLIER`'s own tuning rationale, not observed gameplay.

- **Turn-action Dodge is NOT redundant, but it is dominated (measured, not read off the HUD).** The two
  actions cover different windows: reaction Dodge is available on **100 % of announced strikes** and can
  never be wasted on a non-strike turn, while turn-action Dodge costs the turn action, is lost to any
  non-strike enemy turn, and — because `chooseAITacticalAction` branch 1 reads `player.isBlocking` only —
  does not bend the AI the way a guard does (P(strike) = `aggression`, 0.50–0.95; 0.45 while guarding).
  **The one thing only the turn action can do is answer the telegraphed heavy**, which has no reaction
  row. That niche is real (retreat is the only free alternative and it yields ground), so the action must
  not be removed or renamed; it needs the telegraph to be the case it exists for.

- **Recommendation — policy A, unchanged, price decision deferred.** The contract stays "activation pays
  for the stance": the audit's premise (a charge stranded on a strike that never arrives) does not hold
  for the reaction path, and the two candidates that would move it either change nothing (B) or pay the
  player for failure and make the price unknowable (C). Transition contract to pin: **activate** → 12 SP
  now · **non-strike enemy action** → no window, no charge · **announced strike** → the stance always
  meets an impact · **successful evade** → no further charge · **failed evade** → no refund, full
  unmitigated blow, named by `landedStrikeText` · **unaffordable activation** → refused before the
  reaction claim, announcement left unspent, HUD button disabled by `canAffordDodge` · **stance clears**
  at the top of the fighter's next `executeCombatTurn`. **Unresolved design question for the next phase
  (out of scope here): is Dodge's price loadout-aware, or is the Guard's free stamina credit the lever?**
  Both answers move a number this gate is forbidden to touch.

- **Files/tests a future implementation would touch** (none changed here): `utils/combatCalculations.ts`
  (`planDodgeReaction`, `canAffordDodge`, the price), `DuelScene.tsx` L1298-1355 / L936 / L1005-1018,
  `CombatHUD.tsx` L87 / L318 / L331-336 — the guard's "no cost" label beside the dodge's "−12 SP" is the
  dominance made visible — and `utils/pendingStrike.ts` if a charge ever moved to impact. Suites:
  `phaseC8_83B`, `phaseC8_83D`, `phaseC8_84A`, `phaseC8_84B`, `phaseC8_84D`, `phaseC8_84F`,
  `defensiveBalance`, `phaseC8_82b`, `phaseC8_79C`, `pendingStrike`, `combatActionOrder`.

- **Verified / not verified.** `bun test` over `phaseC8_82b`, `defensiveBalance`, `phaseC8_83B`,
  `phaseC8_83D`, `phaseC8_84A`, `phaseC8_84B`, `phaseC8_84D`, `phaseC8_84F`, `pendingStrike`,
  `combatActionOrder`, `phaseC8_79C`, `combatResponsiveness` → **304 pass / 0 fail** (12 files, 76324
  `expect()`); the full suite was not run. Every combat figure is production helpers plus a throwaway
  deterministic model (container `/tmp` only, never the repo) on the C-8.85A player kit: the *formulas,
  constants and roster* are production, the *player stat block* is inherited from C-8.85A and is an
  assumption, and **no live duel was played**. **No live-duel or Android acceptance is claimed.**

## Dodge/Guard resource balance resolution (Phase C-8.85C — audited, NO production change)

- **Preflight (differs from the brief; preserved, not restored).** Branch `development-focus-strategy`,
  HEAD **`f43d4206519234ea187a2c25d040b341f26c0e5d`** "Append C-8.85B record to AGENTS.md" — one commit
  on top of the brief's expected `af0f7089ef` (C-8.85A), its parent and intact — `git status --porcelain`
  **empty** before and after. Nothing was reset, stashed, amended, committed, pushed, merged or deployed,
  and **no production file was edited**. This record is the phase's only change.

- **Verdict: NEITHER lever can be selected. No production change was made, and the reason is arithmetic
  rather than taste.** The dominance does not sit in Dodge's price (lever A) or in the guard's credit
  (lever B) alone: it sits in the fact that **a reaction Guard is a net stamina SOURCE of 7.7–14.9 SP per
  announced strike while a Dodge is a net SINK of 12**, a 20.5–28.2 SP swing per announcement against
  which Dodge's whole damage advantage is **−0.06…2.97 HP ≈ −0.03…2.8 SP of offence**. A price is
  non-negative and a credit reduction is at most a withdrawal, so the one admissible price band is
  empty and the one admissible multiplier band stops short of the fix.

- **The kit, and what is assumption vs production.** Every formula (`calculateAttackDamage`,
  `calculateHitChance`, `shieldGuardStaminaGain`, `canAffordDodge`, `planDodgeReaction`,
  `chooseAITacticalAction`, `calculateTotalStats`) and the whole roster/catalogue are production; the
  *player stat block* is an assumption, derived by `calculateTotalStats` from one profile
  (`baseStats` str 14 / agi 12 / sta 10 / def 10; `helm_centurion` + `chest_lorica_segmentata` +
  `arms_manica` + `legs_greaves_bronze`) with only the weapon swapped across all 11 catalogue weapons —
  8 opponents × light/heavy = 176 pairs, throwaway scripts in the container's `/tmp` only. Representative
  derived kits: **gladius** block 0.82, def 47, hp 289, pool 120, regen 29.7 (**spatha** 0.85/48/304);
  **shamshir** 0.80/45/299, regen 32.1; shield-less **sicae** 0.40/283, regen 34.5, **titan mace**
  0.75/357, **hoplite spear** 0.45/283.

- **Dodge's damage advantage per announcement** (`hit% × [guard − (1 − 0.88) × dodge]`, both through the
  real formula on the same mitigated blow): gladius **0.27…1.85 HP**, spatha **−0.06…1.18**, shamshir
  **0.43…2.97** — the C-8.85A "0.42–2.21" reproduced on a different kit. Shield-less it is
  **0.69…17.76** (sicae 3.35…15.38, pugio up to 17.76), the archetype split C-8.72B intended, and it survives intact.

- **The guard's credit per announcement**, measured today: **8.45–16.21 SP** (light strikes 12.25–16.21,
  heavies 8.45–11.56 on the gladius kit). It is ≥ the entire Dodge price against **every** opponent and
  every strike type, and it is loadout-independent — a shield-less fighter bracing at 0.40 collects the
  same credit, which is why even the shield-less comparison does not favour Dodge once the credit is
  counted.

- **Break-even Dodge price `C* = ΔHP / HPperSP`**, where one SP is valued per pair at the player's own
  light strike against that opponent (HP/SP **1.09–3.00** on the three shield kits, **1.09–5.22** across
  the catalogue — *measured*, not the 1.9–3.0 first assumed): **gladius 0.20…1.70**, spatha −0.03…0.86, shamshir
  0.16…1.62; shield-less sicae 1.06…7.67, spear 1.17…9.72, pugio up to 12.22. Subtract the credit the
  guard would have paid and **every shield pair goes negative (−13.38…−7.20)**. That is the C-8.85B
  "one flat price cannot serve a ~15× spread" finding, reproduced with a second, independent yardstick.

- **Lever A — loadout-aware Dodge cost: REJECTED, on evidence.** Swept the shield-carrier price over
  0/2/3/4/6/8/12 SP against all 16 shield pairs per kit: **at every price ≥ 2 SP Dodge is worth choosing
  in 0/16 pairs**; only at 0 SP does it win, and then only if the guard's credit is ignored — 16/16 for
  gladius and shamshir, 14/16 for spatha — and 0/16 once it is counted. So the rule that would "work" is **≈0–1.7 SP for shield carriers, 12 SP for
  everyone else** — a free evade, which takes 12 % of the blow where the guard takes 18 %. That hands the
  shield archetype the best block, the only stamina engine **and** the best evade, while a shield-less
  fighter still pays 12 for the same evade: it **reverses the archetype preference** and is a new
  exploit, not a fix. Cost-wise it is not the small lever either: `planDodgeReaction`, `canAffordDodge`,
  `enforceAffordableAIAction` (C-8.84B's downgrade), the `DuelScene` turn-action guard (C-8.84A), the
  `resolveReactionCue` copy, `CombatHUD` and `TurnActionPanel` all read the cost today and would each need
  the weapon threaded in.

- **Lever B — smaller guard stamina credit: REJECTED, on evidence.** Swept `SHIELD_GUARD_REGEN_MULTIPLIER`
  0.5 → 0.4 / 0.3 / 0.2 / 0.1 / 0: the credit falls 11.0–14.1 → 8.8–11.3 → 6.6–8.5 → 4.4–5.6 → 2.2–3.0 →
  0, and `C*` with the credit counted stays **negative at every step but the last** (−1.26…−1.91 at
  ×0.1). At the **extreme of ×0 — a total withdrawal, beyond "modest"** — `C*` reaches only
  **0.51…1.50 SP**, still far below 12, so **B cannot close the gap even at its limit**; a modest step
  (×0.4) moves the swing by ≈2.8 SP per announcement, which is noise against a 20–28 SP swing. It also
  deletes the guard's only recovery — the one credit C-8.70B §R2 and C-8.72B deliberately keep — and it
  does not touch Guard's third advantage, the AI branch.

- **Why Guard wins three ways and Dodge one (all measured).** Guard: costs 0 · credits 8–16 SP per
  announced strike · bends `chooseAITacticalAction` branch 1 — a 2000-point sweep on all eight opponents
  gives **P(attack) 0.50 / 0.60 / 0.75 / 0.45 / 0.85 / 0.60 / 0.90 / 0.95 → 0.45 for every one** (the
  0.45 being a 45 % POWER attack). Dodge: passes 12 % instead of 18 % of the blow. Nothing in a
  non-negative price or a credit trim can outweigh the first three.

- **Capacity, and the paths that did not move.** Pool 120 funds **10** paid dodges at 12 (15 at 8, 20 at
  6, 30 at 4); Guard is unbounded by construction. The affordability contract was re-driven and is
  unchanged: 11 SP → `canAffordDodge` false / `planDodgeReaction` `refused` / AI downgrades `dodge` →
  `shield_block`; 12 SP → `activate`, cost 12, `countsDodge`; a held stance at 0 SP → `reaffirm`, cost 0.
  Non-strike turns never announce, so no reaction is offered and nothing can be charged for them; the
  telegraphed heavy still resolves directly with no reaction row, so **the turn-action Dodge keeps its
  one distinct use** — unaffected by either lever, since both would only move the reaction price or the
  credit.

- **The unresolved design decision, stated for the next phase.** *Is a reaction Guard allowed to be a net
  stamina SOURCE of ≈8–15 SP per announced strike?* As long as it is, the credit alone exceeds the whole
  Dodge price for **every** loadout, so no non-negative price makes Dodge competitive; and as long as the
  price is 12, no credit reduction short of total withdrawal makes it competitive either. The two levers
  are therefore **one joint decision**, which this phase's brief forbids combining — hence no change.

- **Evidence that would resolve it.** (1) A **stated design target**: on what share of announcements each
  stance should be the correct answer (e.g. Dodge optimal on 20–30 % for a shield build and 60–70 %
  shield-less). Without it no price is *right* rather than merely different — every figure above is
  comparative, not a goal. (2) **A live stamina curve**: the model assumes 12 SP ≈ 0.5–0.6 of a light
  strike and that one regen turn (+29.7) funds about two attacks; logging real per-round SP in a device
  duel would replace that assumption with measured data. (3) A **decision on C-8.70B §R2's intent** —
  "raising the guard recovers nothing on its own" — versus the stopped-blow credit it kept: is that
  credit defensive identity, or the leftover that makes Guard the arena's best stamina engine?

- **Regression tests: none added, deliberately.** No production value moved, and every contract this
  phase was asked to lock is already pinned — `phaseC8_84A`/`84B` (player and AI affordability, the
  `shield_block` fallback), `phaseC8_84D`/`84F` (loadout-aware guard feedback), `phaseC8_83B` (free
  reaffirm, no second charge), `defensiveBalance` §C/§D (exactly −12, one debit), `phaseC8_82b` §D
  (Guard ≥ 0, Dodge exactly −12) and §A/§E (evade rate, damage, block mitigation, timings).

- **Verified 2026-10-26** in the dev container: focused defensive set — `bun test` over `defensiveBalance`,
  `phaseC8_82b`, `phaseC8_83B`, `phaseC8_84A`, `phaseC8_84B`, `phaseC8_84D`, `phaseC8_84F`,
  `combatResponsiveness`, `phaseC8_75E`, `combatActionOrder`, `phaseC8_83D`, `playerStrikeWindup` →
  **331 pass / 0 fail** (12 files, 77035 `expect()`); `bun run scripts/combatTests.ts` → **69 passed,
  0 failed**; `bun test` (full) → **3931 pass / 0 fail (140 files)**, 50.7 s; `bun run lint`
  (`tsc --noEmit`) → exit 0; `bun run build` → exit 0 with the startup asset check passing (8 assets);
  `git diff --check` → clean. **Not verified / not attempted:** no live duel, no Android acceptance and
  no preview interaction — every combat figure here is unit-level production helpers plus a
  deterministic EV model (steady-state AI stance mix, light attacks every turn, no potions, one
  attacker), and this phase rendered nothing to look at. **No live-duel or Android acceptance is claimed.**

## Defensive resource economy design gate (Phase C-8.85D — design + evidence, NO production change)

- **Preflight (differs from the brief's expected HEAD; preserved, not restored).** Branch
  `development-focus-strategy`, HEAD **`00c006bf9995bcd3cc1a915c144006d1971b7161`** "Document C-8.85C
  combat balance analysis" — one commit on top of the brief's expected `f43d4206` (C-8.85B), its parent
  and intact. `git status --porcelain` **empty** before and after; nothing was reset, stashed, amended,
  committed, pushed, merged or deployed. The C-8.85A (L10670), C-8.85B (L10753) and C-8.85C (L10862)
  records are present and intact. **No production file, constant, test or asset was edited**; this
  record is the phase's only change.

- **Trace of the credit's origin — what is documented, and what is inference.**
  - *Documented (C-8.70B §R2, `combatCalculations.ts`'s `shieldGuardStaminaGain` doc comment).* The
    problem the rule solved was **the guard's UNCONDITIONAL regen**, not the credit: `applyStaminaRegen`
    ran on *every* Shield Guard turn, so the guard returned full `staminaRegen` while Dodge paid
    `DODGE_STAMINA_COST`. §R2's stated goal was to remove that dominance ("a raised shield that nothing
    hits recovers nothing and the trade-off is real"), and the stopped-blow credit was the **allowance
    deliberately left behind**, not a new engine. It is therefore **a reward for a successful defence**,
    not a temporary measure and not documented as "Guard's defining advantage".
  - *Documented (C-8.72B).* The full credit measured 31.9 SP per blocked exchange against a 12 SP Dodge,
    so `SHIELD_GUARD_REGEN_MULTIPLIER = 0.5` halved it. That record also states the **archetype split**
    that was "always intended": *"The non-shield build's guard (14 damage through 35 % block) stays
    clearly worse than its dodge, which is the archetype split that was always intended."* That is the
    single most important sentence for this phase — see Package D.
  - *Verified in source (not inferred).* `shieldGuardStaminaGain(true, regen)` is called from exactly one
    production site, the resolution's `else if (roll <= hitPct)` → `if (isBlocked)` branch
    (`DuelScene.tsx` L1008). So the credit is paid **only for a blow that actually landed and was
    blocked**: not on a miss, not on an evade, not on a turn where the opponent did not strike, once per
    resolution, and clamped by `applyStaminaRegen` to `staminaMax`. It is **loadout-independent** — the
    call passes no weapon, so a spear or twin-blade "brace" collects the same credit a scutum does.
  - *Inference (mine).* That the current ×0.5 magnitude is a **tuning artefact rather than a derived
    value**: C-8.72B chose 0.5 as "the modest step" that halves the gap, without re-deriving what the
    credit is *for*. Nothing in the code or the records fixes a target for it.

- **The current model's key claims, re-verified with production helpers** (throwaway scripts in the
  container's `/tmp` only; `calculateAttackDamage`, `calculateHitChance`, `shieldGuardStaminaGain`,
  `canAffordDodge`, `chooseAITacticalAction`, `weaponCarriesShield`, `calculateTotalStats`, the whole
  roster and catalogue). Player kit = C-8.85C's (`baseStats` 14/12/10/10 + `helm_centurion`,
  `chest_lorica_segmentata`, `arms_manica`, `legs_greaves_bronze`) → **gladius 0.82 block, def 47,
  hp 289, pool 120, regen 29.7, credit 14.85**; **sicae 0.40, hp 283, regen 34.5, credit 17.25**.
  - **The 0.45 is a real branch, and it is 0.45 for all eight.** `chooseAITacticalAction` tests
    `playerIsBlocking` FIRST, so a guarding player meets `power 0.45 / taunt 0.30 / block 0.25` against
    every opponent, measured over a 4000-point sweep. Three corrections to how C-8.85A/C used it:
    (1) the drop is only 0.50→0.45 for Marcus, 0.60→0.45 for Flaccus/Drusus, 0.75→0.45 for Goliath and
    0.45→0.45 for Cassius — the "85/90/95 → 45" headline quotes the three most aggressive opponents
    only; (2) **every** strike a guarding player faces is a POWER attack (the branch cannot pick a quick
    one), so the guard trades frequency for weight; (3) **30 % of those turns are taunts that refuel the
    OPPONENT (+25 SP)** and 25 % are braces that halve the player's next strike — two costs no earlier
    model counted. A winded guarding opponent gets `rest 0.45 / taunt 0.30 / block 0.25`, i.e. P(strike)
    0, because `enforceAffordableAIAction` downgrades the branch-1 power attack.
  - **Magnitudes reproduce, at the right unit.** Credit is 14.85 (gladius/spatha), 16.05 (shamshir,
    hoplite spear), 17.25 (sicae) per landed blocked blow → **4.77–11.80 SP per announcement** on the
    gladius kit (hit%-weighted) and **3.47–4.68 SP per AI turn** while the turn-action guard is held
    (branch 1 strikes only). C-8.85C's "8.45–16.21" does not reproduce: the 16.21 exceeds the maximum
    possible credit on any shield kit (16.05), and — more importantly — **C-8.85C's own 8.45 lower bound
    contradicts its premise** that the credit is "≥ the entire Dodge price against every opponent".
    **Corrected: the credit is BELOW the 12 SP Dodge price for roughly half the roster**, per
    announcement, and below it for the whole roster per AI turn.
  - **Opportunity cost was missing and it matters more than the credit.** `advance`/`retreat` pay the
    FULL `staminaRegen` (29.7) unconditionally; `rest` +40; `taunt` +25; `shield_block` pays 0 on the turn
    and only the conditional credit afterwards. So the turn-action guard is a **stamina loss versus
    stepping**, and the guard's real value at the turn level is the **attack-rate suppression**
    (28.7 → 3.1 HP per AI turn versus Aurelius), which no earlier model contained.
  - **"No non-negative price is competitive" depends entirely on the unit of account — corrected.** That
    conclusion prices one SP at the player's own light strike (`hp/SP` 2.17 gladius, 3.44 sicae), which
    assumes every SP converts into an attack. Per-bout modelling (which lets a player step to refill)
    shows a reaction Dodge at the SHIPPED 12 SP takes **less** damage than a reaction Guard for the
    shield-less kit in **8/8** pairs (Aurelius 287 v 456 HP) and for the shield kit in **1/8** (Marcus).
    So the verdict is archetype-specific, not global: **Dodge is already the shield-less fighter's
    better damage answer at 12 SP, and is dominated only for shield carriers.**
  - **Structural, not a price problem.** A shield absorbs 82–85 % of a blow, so Dodge's *unique*
    avoidance is `1 − 0.88` v `1 − 0.82` — **0.06 of a blow**, worth 0.57–1.83 HP per announcement
    against a 10.2–23.2 SP swing. No non-negative price can make a 6 % improvement worth a whole attack,
    which is why the price lever is empty **for shields specifically**.

- **Intended role contract (the deliverable of the gate).**
  - **Shield Guard** — the default defensive answer for a shield carrier and the shield archetype's
    identity: free, absorbs 82–85 %, **suppresses the AI's attack rate to 0.45** (and turns its strikes
    heavy, so the mitigation is doing more work), and returns 4.8–11.8 SP per announcement, which is
    **≈ one light attack's cost (12)** — i.e. the credit's job is **TEMPO: it lets an attacking player
    keep a 1.00 attack/turn cadence instead of 0.76–0.88**, measured. Risk: none beyond the turn it
    occupies; it never costs stamina.
  - **Dodge** — the *spend-tempo-to-not-be-hit* answer: 88 % to take **zero**, 12 % to take the blow
    **unmitigated**, 12 SP ≈ one attack. It is the right answer exactly when `blockReduction` is weak and
    the blow is large (shield-less: 1.9–6.5 HP per AI turn saved; 8/8 bouts better than the guard). It is
    the *wrong* answer when your HP is low, because its failure mode is the largest single hit in the
    game.
  - **Turn-action Dodge** — same price, worse information than the reaction dodge, and it is **not**
    the only answer to the telegraphed heavy: a free turn-action Guard covers it too (Goliath landing:
    unarmed **20.4 HP**, turn-guard **3.5**, turn-dodge **2.4** for the gladius kit — 1.1 HP apart, with
    a 39 HP failure tail on the dodge). The correction to C-8.85B is that this niche is real only for
    **shield-less** kits (sicae: guard 10.4 v dodge 2.1, an 8.3 HP difference).
  - **Shield-less defence** — Dodge-first, Guard-second: viable today (sicae wins 7/8 bouts with either),
    but the guard is **better than C-8.72B intended** because it collects the shield's stamina engine
    (Aurelius: guard 456 HP taken, dodge 287).
  - **Measurable targets (derived from the arithmetic, not invented).** (i) *Tempo:* a player who answers
    every announced strike with a guard sustains **≥ 0.95 attacks/turn**; the shipped credit is what
    produces 1.00 versus 0.76–0.88 unguarded. (ii) *Archetype separation:* for a shield-less kit, Dodge
    must beat Guard on bout HP taken in every roster pair (it does, 8/8 at 12 SP); for a shield kit it
    must **not** be required to, because 6 % avoidance cannot pay a whole attack. (iii) *Price sanity:*
    the Dodge price stays ≤ one light attack (12 v 8–14 across the catalogue), which is the only value
    the HUD can teach in one line. **No win-rate or action-frequency target is proposed** — nothing in
    the repo supports one.

- **The four packages, measured (bout = player attacks whenever affordable, else steps; reaction guard
  or reaction dodge on every announcement; expected values, no RNG).**
  | package | gladius: Aurelius | gladius: Valéria | sicae: Aurelius | sicae: Drusus |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | **A** current (credit, 12 SP dodge) | 197 HP / 38 t / WIN | 69 / 22 / WIN | 456 / 28 / LOSS | 73 / 17 / WIN |
  | **B** credit removed | 259 / 50 / WIN | 84 / 27 / WIN | 521 / 32 / LOSS | 78 / 18 / WIN |
  | **C** credit on a stopped HEAVY blow only | 233 / 45 / WIN | 78 / 25 / WIN | 472 / 29 / LOSS | 78 / 18 / WIN |
  | **D** credit only when the defender carries a shield | **197 / 38 / WIN (identical to A)** | 69 / 22 | **521 / 32 (identical to B)** | 78 / 18 |
  - **A** keeps the tempo engine and the endgame margin (92 of 289 HP spare against Aurelius). Its cost
    is the one this gate exists to name: a stamina engine that pays every loadout.
  - **B** flips **no** verdict anywhere and is smaller than feared — the gladius kit still wins 8/8 — but
    it costs **+62 HP and +12 turns** against Aurelius (margin 92 → 30) and +15/+5/+6 HP against
    Valéria/Drusus/Ignis: it spends the shield's identity to buy a consistency it cannot use.
  - **C** lands between A and B for everyone and has an elegant property — the turn-action guard's credit
    is **untouched**, because branch 1's only strike is already a power attack, so the conditional bites
    only on the free reaction refund. Rejected on *legibility*: it makes the refund depend on a
    distinction the HUD does not currently teach (the cue does name the strike type, but the tactic grid
    says only "SP on block").
  - **D is the smallest coherent alternative, and the trace is what reveals it.** Every piece of copy
    around the credit became loadout-aware in C-8.84F (`weaponCarriesShield`, "braces behind their
    shield."), the action is called **Shield** Guard, the HelpModal says "SP on block" — and the credit
    alone still ignores the weapon. D is also **provably zero-risk for the shield archetype**: the
    gladius and spatha kits are HP-identical to A in all eight pairs, because they already carry a
    shield. For the shield-less kits D equals B (no verdict flips; ≤ 15 % more HP taken) and it restores
    C-8.72B's documented split — their guard stops paying them for a shield they do not have, so Dodge
    becomes their best answer by the margin it already had (287 v 521 against Aurelius).

- **Device evidence, and its limits.** **No physical Android device is available in this session, and no
  live duel was played.** The container renders the arena through SwiftShader at ~1–2 fps, which cannot
  produce reaction-timed input; the only observations used from it are that the dev stack serves
  (HTTP 200) and that the sources read as recorded. Every number above is **unit-level production
  helpers plus a deterministic EV model**, and the model **assumes** one attacker, no potions, no
  withdraw, the AI's own stamina ignored (the AI also collects the guard credit when it blocks — not
  modelled), light attacks only for the player, and an AI action mix derived analytically from the
  shipped branch weights and confirmed by a 4000-point sweep. **The cheapest experiment that would
  separate A from D:** one gladius/scutum fighter and one twin-blade fighter, each against **Drusus**
  (moderate aggression 0.60, block 0.75) and **Aurelius** (0.95), 20 AI turns each, logging per exchange
  — incoming damage, dodge success/failure, stamina before/after, credit per stopped blow, the AI's
  action type, and whether the player ever could not afford the next light attack. D predicts **identical
  numbers for the shield fighter** and a **measurably worse stamina curve (≈ −4 SP per announced strike)
  with no change in bout HP taken** for the twin-blade fighter; A predicts the two fighters stay
  indistinguishable on stamina. A and C are separated by one number only: credit per **quick** strike
  stopped (A > 0, C = 0). A live Android capture would also settle the 700 ms wind-up read and the
  one-handed reachability of both reaction buttons, which are still open from C-8.70B.

- **Recommendation — Package D, and nothing else in this phase.** Guard stays free, 82–85 % absorbing,
  AI-suppressing, and credits its carrier; **Dodge stays at 12 SP and 88 %**; the credit is paid only to
  a fighter whose weapon carries a shield. Dodge keeps a real job for shields (the unannounced telegraphed
  heavy, and bursts) without being asked to beat an 82 % block, and becomes the shield-less fighter's
  default — which is what C-8.72B said it always was. **Stopping rule:** if the twin-blade experiment
  above does not show the predicted stamina shortfall with unchanged bout HP, D's premise (the credit is
  the shield-less fighter's crutch) is wrong and the phase should be re-opened rather than implemented;
  conversely, if the shield fighter's numbers move at all, the implementation is wrong, because D is
  mathematically a no-op for shields.

- **What a future implementation would change (NOT done here).** No constant moves. `shieldGuardStaminaGain`
  gains a loadout-aware argument (or, more cheaply, its one call site in `DuelScene.tsx` L1008 passes
  `weaponCarriesShield(defender.loadout.weapon) && defender.stats.staminaRegen`), and
  `TurnActionPanel`'s static `<span>SP on block</span>` (L299) becomes loadout-aware through the existing
  `shieldGuardFeedback`/`weaponCarriesShield` seam so a spear fighter is not promised stamina it will not
  get. **Regression risks:** `defensiveBalance` (§A's multiplier and clamp arithmetic),
  `combatResponsiveness` §A (the 24 → 12 pins), `phaseC8_82b` §D (Guard ≥ 0, Dodge exactly −12),
  `phaseC8_84F` (the copy seam), and `scripts/combatTests.ts`, which reads the credit directly. **Smallest
  validating matrix:** those six plus one new suite pinning (i) shielded → 14.85/16.05/17.25 unchanged,
  (ii) `spear`/`dual_blades`/`mace` → 0 while the mitigation, the AI branch and every price stay
  byte-identical, (iii) the panel copy per loadout, and (iv) the four bout projections in the table above
  as the design's regression fixture.

- **Verified / not verified.** Focused `bun test` over `defensiveBalance`, `phaseC8_82b`, `phaseC8_83B`,
  `phaseC8_84A`, `phaseC8_84B`, `phaseC8_84D`, `phaseC8_84F`, `combatResponsiveness` → **230 pass / 0
  fail (8 files, 75920 expect())** — run because this phase changed no production file, to show the
  baseline it reasons about is intact. The full suite was not run (read-only design gate; CI owns it).
  **No live-duel, no Android and no visual acceptance is claimed**, and none of the four packages was
  implemented.

## Shield-specific Guard stamina credit (Phase C-8.85E — implemented)

- **Preflight (differs from the brief's expected HEAD; preserved, not restored).** Branch
  `development-focus-strategy`, starting HEAD **`404d8ea3a708affe1cb99384cfddd7bba4cd89a8`** "Update
  shield-specific credit logic in AGENTS.md" — ONE commit on top of the brief's expected
  `00c006bf9995bcd3cc1a915c144006d1971b7161` (C-8.85D), its parent and intact; that commit adds the
  C-8.85D record verbatim (178 lines, `AGENTS.md` only), i.e. the previous phase's own uncommitted work
  was committed by the platform at the end of that turn — nothing else. `git status --porcelain` **empty**
  before the work. The C-8.85A (L10670), C-8.85B (L10753), C-8.85C (L10862) and C-8.85D (L10975) records
  are present and were re-read; nothing was reset, stashed, amended, discarded, merged, pushed or
  deployed, and the existing `AGENTS.md` content is preserved below this section unedited.

- **Trace of the credit before the change, verified in source.**
  - The rule lives in ONE pure helper, `combatCalculations.ts`'s `shieldGuardStaminaGain(didStopBlow,
    regen)` = `didStopBlow ? regen * SHIELD_GUARD_REGEN_MULTIPLIER : 0` (0.5), clamped by
    `applyStaminaRegen` to `staminaMax`.
  - It has exactly ONE production call site: the resolution's `else if (roll <= hitPct)` →
    `if (isBlocked)` branch of `DuelScene.tsx` (the point at which a blow is considered successfully
    stopped). `isBlocked` is `defender.isBlocking`, so a landed blow against a held guard is always
    blocked; the credit is therefore paid once per **resolved, landed, blocked** strike — never on a
    miss, never on an evade, and once per resolution rather than per callback.
  - Player and AI defenders share that one site: `isActorPlayer ? setOpp(...) : setPlayer(...)` — the
    defender is whichever fighter is not the attacker. **Both were loadout-blind.**
  - `defender.loadout.weapon` (a required `WeaponItem`) is available at that point and was already read
    there for `blockReduction` and for the C-8.84F shield-accuracy of the blocked-strike line.
  - The canonical shield classification already exists: `guardFeedback.ts`'s
    `weaponCarriesShield(weapon)` — the one detector the three feedback builders and the rendered scutum
    (`GladiatorMesh`) also use. **No second definition was created.**

- **The change — three production/test lines and nothing else.** `shieldGuardStaminaGain` gains a third,
  defaulted parameter `carriesShield = true` and returns 0 when it is false; a new pure predicate
  `carriesShieldForGuardCredit(weapon)` in the same module asks `weaponCarriesShield` and adds only the
  presence requirement (an unresolved weapon is not a shield, so a partial loadout cannot mint stamina);
  and the one call site passes
  `carriesShieldForGuardCredit(defender.loadout?.weapon)`. The default keeps the helper's other callers
  (`scripts/combatTests.ts` and four suites that assert the SHIELDED formula) describing what they always
  described — the shielded magnitude — while no live fighter can reach it, because the only production
  caller passes the answer explicitly. **The authoritative eligibility point is therefore the helper's
  contract plus that single call site; nothing is duplicated across callers.** The shield rule is asked,
  never restated: the credit module contains no `includes('shield')` and no `=== 'sword_shield'`.

- **What did not move, and is asserted unchanged.** The shielded formula, multiplier (0.5) and clamp;
  block mitigation and the damage formula; `DODGE_EVADE_CHANCE` 0.88 and `DODGE_STAMINA_COST` 12;
  activation-time charging and held-stance reaffirmation (`planDodgeReaction`); the AI affordability
  guards (`canAffordDodge`, `enforceAffordableAIAction`); turn-action Dodge; attack costs; AI weights;
  taunt/step recovery; and every shield-feedback string and HUD label.

- **Regression suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_85E.test.ts`** — 23 tests / 188 assertions across 9 sections,
  running the real helpers over the real catalogue and roster: **A** eligibility (every `sword_shield`
  weapon eligible, every `spear`/`dual_blades`/`mace` weapon not, `undefined`/`null`/`{}`/unknown-type/
  blank-name all ineligible, and eligibility shown to equal `weaponCarriesShield` for all 10 catalogue
  weapons plus a source check that the credit module implements no second rule); **B** the shielded credit
  unchanged (14.85 for the C-8.85D gladius kit regen 29.7, and the pre-existing two-argument contract
  12 / 2.5 / 15.95); **C** a shield-less defender earning 0 for the same stopped blow, its stamina left
  exactly where it was, and its `blockReduction` still absorbing; **D** the unblocked strike (both
  loadouts) plus the unblocked resolution branch carrying no stamina write; **E** the evade branch and
  the `shield_block` stance branches carrying no credit, 12 SP / 0.88 re-pinned, `canAffordDodge`
  thresholds intact; **F** exactly one credit call site inside `if (isBlocked)`, `guardGain` computed
  once and applied once through the two mutually exclusive defender arms, and one application adding
  exactly one credit rather than two; **G** the cap for both loadouts (including a shield-less defender
  never being pushed over it) and malformed regen crediting nothing; **H** the resolution reading the
  DEFENDER's weapon at that one site, every one of the 8 opponents resolving under the same rule
  (`sword_shield` iff eligible), and a player and an AI carrying the same weapon treated identically;
  **I** the shared feedback seam — shield wording exactly when eligible, over every catalogue weapon,
  with the shielded strings byte-identical to the shipped ones.

- **Two existing pins were rebased, not weakened.** `defensiveBalance`'s "the rule lives in the shared
  helper and nowhere else" and `phaseC8_84F`'s "the guard credit is still the blocked branch's only
  stamina write" both asserted the literal single-line call
  `shieldGuardStaminaGain(true, defender.stats.staminaRegen)`; each now matches the same call with its new
  eligibility argument (a regex over the same two unchanged inputs), so the claims — one call site, inside
  the blocked branch, the fighter's own stat — are intact and the eligibility argument is now positively
  pinned too. No assertion was deleted or relaxed anywhere, and the 2-argument form remains valid and
  asserted in `defensiveBalance`, `combatResponsiveness`, `phaseC8_84A`, `phaseC8_75B` and `phaseC8_75F`.

- **Before → after, measured with production helpers** (throwaway model in the container's `/tmp` only;
  `calculateTotalStats`, `calculateAttackDamage`, `calculateHitChance`, `shieldGuardStaminaGain`,
  `carriesShieldForGuardCredit`, `applyStaminaRegen`, the real catalogue and roster). Player kit = the
  C-8.85D one (`baseStats` 14/12/10/10 + `helm_centurion`, `chest_lorica_segmentata`, `arms_manica`,
  `legs_greaves_bronze`); opponents' weapons resolved by `weaponType`; a held guard stops every landed
  blow, so credit per announcement = hit% × credit and per AI turn = 0.45 × that.

  | quantity | gladius + scutum | twin sicae |
  |---|---|---|
  | carries a shield / `blockReduction` | yes / 0.82 | **no** / 0.40 |
  | DEF 47, HP 289, pool 120, regen 29.7 | — | DEF 45, HP 283, pool 120, regen 34.5 |
  | credit per stopped blow | **14.85 → 14.85** | **17.25 → 0** |
  | vs Drusus: blocked 5 v unblocked 25 (80 % mitigation) | credit/announcement 8.91 → 8.91 | blocked 15 v 26 (42.3 %): 9.14 → **0** |
  | vs Aurelius: blocked 9 v unblocked 52 (82.7 %) | 9.95 → 9.95; per AI turn 4.48 → 4.48 | blocked 32 v 53 (39.6 %): 10.35 → **0**; per AI turn 4.66 → **0** |
  | stamina over 8 guarded exchanges from 60 SP (vs Aurelius) | 95.82 → 95.82 (**Δ 0**) | 97.26 → 60.00 (**Δ −37.26**) |
  | light attacks affordable after those exchanges | 7 → 7 | 10 → 6 |
  | cap trace from 115 SP | 119.48, 120, 120 … (unchanged) | 119.66 → **115 flat** (no credit, no clamp pressure) |

  So the shield archetype is **numerically identical** — C-8.85D predicted a mathematical no-op for
  shields and the model confirms it to the SP — while the shield-less brace stops paying itself and
  becomes, as C-8.72B documented, the weaker defensive answer than its own Dodge. Those magnitudes
  reproduce C-8.85D's per-announcement band (4.77–11.80) and per-AI-turn band (3.47–4.68).
  **Assumptions:** one attacker, no potions, no withdraw, player guards every AI turn (P(strike) 0.45,
  branch-1 strikes are power attacks), a held guard stops every landed blow, defender at half stamina,
  expected values rather than sampled RNG, and the AI's own stamina, taunts and braces not modelled (the
  AI also collects the credit when it blocks, and now only if it carries a shield — Mace and
  dual-blade opponents no longer do).

## Guard credit API safety and loadout-aware tactic copy (Phase C-8.85F — implemented)

- **Preflight.** Branch `development-focus-strategy`, starting HEAD
  `707097ac818944f6f8ea664fd921babf0c1e6ea4`, `git status --porcelain` **empty** before the work; the
  C-8.85E implementation and its record are present in that history. Nothing was reset, stashed, amended,
  discarded, merged, pushed or deployed, and the changes are left uncommitted.

- **The API defect, and the fix.** `combatCalculations.ts`'s `shieldGuardStaminaGain(didStopBlow, regen,
  carriesShield = true)` defaulted eligibility to shielded, so a future caller that omitted the third
  argument would silently inherit a shield it may not carry. The parameter is now **required** at the type
  boundary and the helper fails closed on its value: `if (carriesShield !== true) return 0;` refuses
  `undefined` (an omitted argument), `null`, and every truthy non-boolean a mistaken caller could pass
  (`'true'`, `1`, `{}`, a loadout object). The shielded formula, its ×0.5 multiplier, the regen sanity
  guard and the `applyStaminaRegen` cap are untouched, so a shield carrier's credit is byte-identical to
  C-8.72B and C-8.85E: 14.85 SP for the C-8.85D gladius kit (regen 29.7) and 0 for a shield-less loadout.
  `carriesShieldForGuardCredit` already failed closed (an unresolved weapon is not a shield) and is
  unchanged; it remains the ONE eligibility rule and still asks the canonical `weaponCarriesShield`, so no
  second shield classification was created.

- **Every caller updated explicitly, no permissive default added.** The single production call site in
  `DuelScene.tsx` already passed `carriesShieldForGuardCredit(defender.loadout?.weapon)` and needed no
  change. The seven test/script files that described the SHIELDED formula (the convention every suite uses
  for the plain helper contract) now pass `true` explicitly: `scripts/combatTests.ts` (4 calls),
  `combatResponsiveness.test.ts` (13), `defensiveBalance.test.ts` (13), `phaseC8_82b.test.ts` (4),
  `phaseC8_85E.test.ts` (3), `phaseC8_84A.test.ts` (2), `phaseC8_75B.test.ts` (1). Every one of those
  assertions is the same value it was before — the argument is added, nothing is relaxed.

- **The tactic-grid copy.** The surface was `TurnActionPanel.tsx`'s Shield Guard card, whose footer paired
  `{blockReduction}% Absorb` with an unconditional `SP on block`. It now asks the SAME predicate the engine
  credits with — `carriesShieldForGuardCredit(weapon)` on the fighter's own equipped weapon — and renders
  `SP on block` (unchanged wording, accurate) for a shield carrier and `No SP credit` in neutral ink for a
  shield-less loadout. The absorb percentage, the `NO COST` badge, the `Brace to absorb N% of incoming
  damage.` description and the formal action name **Shield Guard** are untouched: the stance, its
  mitigation and its zero cost apply to every loadout, so only the promise of stamina changed. The card
  shows the player's own loadout and no AI card exists, so there is no second surface to keep in step.
  `HelpModal.tsx` carried the equivalent generic promise ("the guard recovers stamina only when it
  actually stops a blow"); it now reads "a shield-bearing guard recovers stamina only when it actually
  stops a blow", which is accurate for both loadouts without giving the manual loadout state.

- **Regression suite: `src/utils/phaseC8_85F.test.ts`** — 22 tests / 210 assertions across 5 sections.
  **A** the API (omitted → 0, `undefined`/`null` → 0, eight truthy non-booleans → 0, explicit `false` → 0,
  and the refusal is a finite zero rather than NaN or a throw); **B** the shielded credit unchanged
  (0.5 multiplier, 14.85 / 17.25 / 12 / 2.5 / 0.5 / 15.95, the unstopped and malformed cases, the cap) and
  the shield-less credit zero with the stamina left where it was, plus every catalogue weapon's credit
  shown to equal `weaponCarriesShield`; **C** the contract in source (no defaulted eligibility parameter,
  the `!== true` guard present, exactly one production call site with the explicit predicate, the credit
  still only inside `if (isBlocked)`, and no `=== 'sword_shield'` / `includes('shield')` in the credit
  module or the panel); **D** the tactic grid **rendered with `react-dom/server`** (the `phaseC8_84D`
  convention) for a shield and for every shield-less weapon — the Shield Guard card carries `SP on block`
  iff `weaponCarriesShield`, and the agreement is asserted across the whole catalogue, with the action
  name, `NO COST`, the absorb line and the enabled state unchanged; **E** what did not move (Dodge's 12 SP
  and 0.88, `canAffordDodge`, `planDodgeReaction`'s free held-stance reaffirmation and single reaction
  charge, the three guard-feedback builders' wording, and the help copy).

- **Verified in the dev container** (`docker compose -f docker-compose.base44.yml exec -T web …`):

## Defensive-balance test contract reconciliation (Phase C-8.85H — implemented, tests only)

- **Preflight.** Branch `development-focus-strategy`, HEAD **`24ca693448bfea3aff3320712dbede1e331dd6e0`**,
  `git status --short` **empty**. **There is no C-8.85G record in this file**: that phase was a
  read-only audit, so its findings live only in its chat report (this phase is the follow-up it
  recommended). The audit's premise — "the uncommitted C-8.85F state" — was also stale: C-8.85F is
  **committed as HEAD** (`24ca693`, on top of `707097a`), so the audited code is the committed code.

- **The stale contract, stated exactly.** `defensiveBalance.test.ts` carried
  `const NON_SHIELD_REGEN = 37.5` documented as *"the measured `staminaRegen` of the non-shield
  (pugio 0.35 block) build"*, and a test named **`a non-shield build is credited the same
  proportional half`** asserting `shieldGuardStaminaGain(true, 37.5, true) === 18.75`. Since
  C-8.85E a Pugio earns **0**, so the assertion held only because it hardcoded the eligibility
  argument `true` — the suite asserted the *opposite* of production under a shield-less label. That
  is a false statement about shipped behaviour in the one file a future balance pass would read, and
  it is what this phase corrected. **No gameplay was retuned:** `combatCalculations.ts`,
  `DuelScene.tsx`, `TurnActionPanel.tsx`, `HelpModal.tsx`, every balance constant, every AI weight
  and the save format are byte-identical; the phase's only file is
  **`src/utils/defensiveBalance.test.ts`** (+69 / −6).

- **The corrected expectation, four tests replacing the one.** The regen numbers are now named and
  documented as **helper INPUTS, never proof of eligibility** (`SHIELDLESS_PUGIO_REGEN` 37.5;
  `SHIELDLESS_SICAE_REGEN` 34.3 = `12 + 16×0.8 + 10×0.4 + 5.5`), and eligibility comes from the
  canonical `carriesShieldForGuardCredit` — the same predicate production resolution credits with —
  read over real catalogue weapons via a `weaponById()` helper. §A grew 6 → 9 tests:
  1. **a shield-bearing build still earns the audited half-regen credit** — gladius / spatha /

  2. **a shield-less Pugio build earns NO credit for the same stopped blow** — `dagger_pugio` is
     `eligible === false` and pays **0**, while the identical 37.5 pays **18.75** when eligibility is

  3. **a shield-less Sicae build earns NO credit** — `getWeaponByType('dual_blades')` is

  4. **an unblocked blow credits nothing whatever the shield eligibility** — swept over **all 11

  regen both halve exactly` uses `true`; `an unstopped blow, a miss and malformed regen credit nothing`

  and nowhere else` are untouched). Nothing was weakened to make the file pass, and the suite's own
  §A summary line now states that since C-8.85E/F only a shield-bearing loadout earns the credit.

- **A repo sweep confirms no other stale claim was left**: the only remaining "shield-less" strings in
