## Living City landmark signage (L17B — implemented; Android acceptance PENDING)

- **What shipped.** The nine delivered landmark sign GLBs (`public/signs/<id>/<id>.glb`) are mounted
  into their own city buildings through ONE shared component, `src/components/3d/city/LandmarkSign.tsx`,
  driven by ONE typed data map, `src/data/landmarkSigns.ts`. Each building mounts it as a single
  `<LandmarkSign id="…" />` child of its root group, so a sign moves with its building. The Grand
  Colosseum keeps its own `ColosseumSignPrototype` mount (Phase 29.3D, beside the entrance steps at
  scale 1.35) and is deliberately **not** re-signed. **That GLB is not a plate-only asset** — L17D
  corrected this record: `grand_colosseum.glb` carries the same full post-and-bracket assembly as the
  other nine (13 meshes: plate, post, post base, post cap, arm, brace, scroll and six chain links),
  and `ColosseumSignPrototype` renders `gltf.scene` unmodified.

- **The assets are floor-standing post signs, not wall plaques — and they are cut-out plates.** Every
  GLB shares one construction: an iron post (local X −1.12 … −0.72) with a bracket arm at Y 2.53 … 2.63
  from which the plate hangs at Y 0.79 … 2.34 on six chain links, 2.86 tall over a 0.398 depth
  envelope. Nothing is textured, so the lettering is the plate's own silhouette — which is why the
  Colosseum sign's dark walnut backing panel is reused verbatim (margin 0.03, depth 0.015, centre
  Y 1.565 / Z −0.060; width per sign = `plateWidth + 2 × margin`, so no plate is stretched). Only the
  plate's X extent differs per sign (0.878 … 1.265) and it is measured, not assumed.

- **Mounting rule, and the two places it needed a judgement call.** Every sign stands on the apron of
  the facade the player enters — the door / awning / portico face — turned so the plate's readable
  front (local +Z, the thick side at Z 0.061) faces that approach, and offset along the facade so the
  doorway's walking line stays clear. Measured clearances to the building's own collider: Tavern 0.501,
  Forge 0.501, Store 0.751, Library 0.401, Medical 0.351, Barracks 0.351, Academy 0.351, Veteran Hall
  0.151 (its plate stands just off the 0.16-high bottom step), Training Hall 3.201 (its apron is the
  veranda, which — like every building's posts and awnings — carries no collider; the plate is 0.55
  from the veranda's outer edge). Two faces are bespoke rather than the doorway's: the **Gladiator
  Academy** reads SOUTH off its undecorated south frontage (its west portal is a 3.9-wide pocket
  between two columns and the `[25.5, −23]` arrival sits on that walk line), and every sign on a
  building whose fast-travel arrival is on another face (Barracks: arrival east, door south; Veteran
  Hall: arrival north, door south) stays on the **entrance** face rather than a blank rear wall.

- **Coordinates live in the building's own frame.** `position` / `rotationY` are local to the building
  root group, with `buildingRoot` / `buildingYaw` recorded so world placement is derivable:
  `world = root + R_y(yaw) · local`, `worldYaw = yaw + rotationY`. Only the Training Hall is rotated
  (parent yaw +π/2), which is why its local rotation is 0 while it reads east. In this city +X is
  east, −X west, +Z south, −Z north.

- **Nothing was added to the movement or interaction systems.** The signs are decoration with no
  collider — exactly like the buildings' barrels, crates and benches — so `CITY_COLLIDERS` is still
  **142 colliders / 32 rectangles / 46 `colo-*`**, `HUB_LOCATIONS` and `FAST_TRAVEL_ARRIVALS` are still
  **21 each**, and `cityClock.ts`, the visitor systems, the save format and every gameplay module are
  untouched. `src/data/landmarkSigns.ts` imports nothing at all, and `LandmarkSign.tsx` imports only
  react / three / drei / its own data — plus, since L17D, the project's shared
  `ThreeComponentErrorBoundary`: no per-frame work, no lights, no animation, no eager preload of the
  other models. Each sign owns its `Suspense`, so a loading GLB cannot blank its building, and (L17D)
  its own error boundary, so a FAILED GLB cannot blank the district either.

- **Draw-call cost, stated honestly.** Each GLB is 13 meshes (plate, post, base, cap, arm, brace,
  scroll, six chain links) plus the backing panel — **14 draw calls and ~4.6–5.2 k triangles per sign,
  ≈126 draw calls and ≈45 k triangles for the nine**. That is the same construction the shipped
  Colosseum sign already renders, and the assets were reused unmodified as instructed; a future
  optimisation (not done here) could merge each sign's meshes by its two materials (plate gold +
  dark iron) to 3 draws per sign.

- **Regression suite: `src/utils/l17bLandmarkSigns.test.ts` — 28 tests / 2 271 `expect()` calls.**
  §A the data (nine unique ids, nine stable `/signs/<id>/<id>.glb` paths, explicit finite mounting
  parameters, facing derived from the world yaw, plate front pointing away from the building, per-sign
  backing widths); §B the assets (every GLB re-parsed with `@gltf-transform/core`: the plate's width,
  its 0.79 … 2.34 Y band, its X centring, the backing sitting behind the plate's back face, the
  assembly's 0 ground contact / 2.86 height / 0.398 depth); §C the mounts (exactly one
  `<LandmarkSign>` per target building and never more than one in any city file, the Colosseum's own
  sign still mounted once, every sign footprint disjoint from all 142 colliders, each sign flanking
  its own facade inside a measured 0.15 … 3.5 band, inside the movement boundary, and clear of every
  hub centre and arrival); §D the contract (the data module imports nothing, the component imports
  only five specifiers — L17D added the shared 3D boundary — the registry/hub radii are what
  C-8.64B/C-8.47 left, no sign covers a hub).

- **Verified 2026-10-26** in the dev container: focused `bun test src/utils/l17bLandmarkSigns.test.ts`
  → **28 pass / 0 fail**; relevant city/collision regressions
  `bun test src/utils/phaseC8_{47,64a,64b,65}.test.ts src/utils/cityClock.test.ts` → **159 pass /
  0 fail**; `bun test` → **4 056 pass / 0 fail (145 files)**; `bun run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) → exit 0;
  `bun run build` → exit 0 (the pre-existing >500 kB chunk warning only, startup assets ✓);
  `git diff --check` → clean. The checkout was `development-focus-strategy` at `f8dae23aa0` with an
  empty `git status` before the first edit; the phase's diff is 9 building components (2 lines each)
  plus the three new files.

- **Live evidence, and what it does and does not prove.** Driven in the preview browser: title → PLAY
  → character creation → the 3D city hub, and the network log shows **all ten sign GLBs requested and
  answered HTTP 200** (`grand_colosseum`, `city_tavern`, `smithing_forge`, `general_store`,
  `training_hall`, `records_library`, `arena_medical`, `gladiator_barracks`, `gladiator_academy`,
  `veteran_hall`) with **0 failed requests** — i.e. the city scene really instantiated all nine signs.
  **No legible frame of a sign was obtained**, and that is an environment limit: the sandbox has no GPU
  (SwiftShader, ~1.5–2 fps in the hub), the preview browser restarts from the title screen on every
  fresh load with **no saved profile**, and each entry costs a character-creation pass plus the
  four-to-five-hold gladiator oath (`OATH_HOLD_MS` 1 500) before the player can walk or fast-travel —
  more than one script budget. **Android visual acceptance is therefore PENDING** for: each sign's
  approach-side reading, its legibility at a plausible distance, facade/awning clearance, ground and
  navigation clearance, whether it reads as belonging to that building, and whether nine extra
  cut-out plates cost frame time on the target GPU.

- **Reproduction steps for the device pass — inspect the ARRIVAL VIEW and the DOOR APPROACH.** Fast
  travel does **not** put the player on each sign's own approach. `FAST_TRAVEL_ARRIVALS`
  (`src/utils/cityCollisions.ts`) lands the player at the nearest verified collision-free point outside
  the building — frequently a corner or an edge of a facade, and on three buildings on the opposite side
  of the building from the sign. **The plates are oriented toward their building's door approach** (the
  door / awning / portico / veranda face — `position` + `rotationY` in `src/data/landmarkSigns.ts`), not
  toward the fast-travel point, so an arriving player can find the plate edge-on or out of sight. The
  Android tester should therefore look at BOTH: (a) the view from the fast-travel arrival, and (b) the
  walk up to the building's door, where the plate is meant to read.

  | building | plate faces | fast-travel arrival (world XZ) | arrival → plate, XZ | arrival off the plate's front axis* |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | The Golden Palm Tavern | east | `[-10, 14]` | 2.93 | 73° — beside the plate, nearly edge-on |
  | Imperial Smithing Forge | west | `[11.5, 2.6]` | 3.37 | 72° — beside the plate, nearly edge-on |
  | Bazaar & General Store | west | `[17, −5]` | 2.01 | 84° — beside the plate, edge-on |
  | Ludus Training Hall | east | `[-18, 2]` | 8.33 | 24° — the one roughly front-on arrival; the sign sits across the yard |
  | Records & Lore Library | south | `[23.1, −26]` | 2.56 | 78° — beside the plate, nearly edge-on |
  | Arena Medical House | south | `[-29, −9]` | 7.61 | 164° — arrival is NORTH, door south: the building is between them |
  | Gladiator Barracks | south | `[-22, −14]` | 4.47 | 144° — arrival is EAST: the sign is met rounding the south-east corner |
  | Gladiator Ludus Academy | south | `[25.5, −23]` | 2.81 | 94° — arrival is the north-west corner: the south frontage is in view but the plate is edge-on |
  | Veteran Gladiator Hall | south | `[-24, −29]` | 7.95 | 159° — arrival is NORTH, door south: the sign is read walking round |

  *Every table figure is a **source-derived calculation, not a rendered visual measurement**:
  `landmarkSignWorldMount()` plus the `FAST_TRAVEL_ARRIVALS` entry. "Off the front axis" is the angle
  between the plate's readable front — world `(sin yaw, cos yaw)` from `worldYaw = buildingYaw +
  rotationY` — and the line from the plate to the arrival: 0° square-on, 90° edge-on, beyond 90° the
  arrival is behind the plate. Distances are XZ only, plate origin to arrival. Sign-relative placements
  (Tavern 2.8 NORTH of its door's centre, Forge at the SOUTH end of the colonnade front, Barracks post
  0.48 clear of the east jamb, …) are recorded per sign in `src/data/landmarkSigns.ts`, which is the file
  to edit if a mount needs moving.

## Living City landmark signage reliability (L17D — implemented; Android acceptance PENDING)

- **Scope.** Three narrow corrections to L17B/L17C — individual sign-load isolation, one measured
  placement defect, and factual documentation — with **no** redesign: no reorientation toward
  arrival points, no scale change toward the Colosseum prototype, no GLB shadow enablement, no
  shadow/material-sharing infrastructure, no lighting, clock, gameplay, save, collider, hub, arrival,
  visitor or combat change, and no new sign or building. Preflight: `development-focus-strategy` at
  `c82a1121a8` with an **empty `git status`**; the diff left uncommitted for review.

- **Priority A — a failed sign is now local to its sign.** `useGLTF` rejects on a missing or corrupt
  GLB and React re-throws that rejection during render; before this phase the nearest boundary above
  `LandmarkSign` was `CityHubScene`'s single `componentName="CityArchitecturalDistricts"` boundary, so
  **one failed sign unmounted the whole architectural district**. `LandmarkSign.tsx` now renders
  `<ThreeComponentErrorBoundary componentName={\`LandmarkSign:<id>\`} fallback={null}>` **outside** its
  `Suspense`: `Suspense` still owns loading, the existing project-standard 3D boundary owns load and
  render failures, and a failed sign renders nothing while every other building, prop, sign and
  collider is untouched. No global handler, no second retry mechanism and no change to the district's
  own fallback for unrelated components. The boundary's `state` has exactly one transition
  (`getDerivedStateFromError`) and no `componentDidUpdate`/`setState`/`componentWillReceiveProps`, so
  a permanently missing asset cannot loop: it stays tripped for the life of the mount. Still
  decoration — `CITY_COLLIDERS` is **142 / 32 rects / 46 `colo-*`**, `HUB_LOCATIONS` and
  `FAST_TRAVEL_ARRIVALS` are **21 each**.

- **Priority B — the Barracks post no longer stands inside its own doorway.** Re-derived from
  `GladiatorBarracks.tsx` and `ClassicalArchitecture.tsx`'s own literals (`ClassicalDoorway` at

## Living City visitor herald (L21B — implemented; visual/device acceptance PENDING)

- **Preflight.** Branch `development-focus-strategy`, HEAD **`8c464116543007a77b534dbcecafe4cc99339ab9`**
  (the audit's baseline), `git status --short` empty and `git diff` empty. Nothing was reset, stashed or
  discarded; the work is additive on that tip. No deploy, no push, no commit, and the running `web`
  container was not restarted.

- **What shipped — the herald calls the day's visitors.** `src/utils/visitorHerald.ts` is a pure module:
  `visitorHeraldCry(visitor)` (the established `The herald cries: …` voice, using the catalogue's `name`
  and `title` only), `visitorHeraldKey(day, visitorId)` = `${day}:${visitorId}`, and
  `createVisitorHeraldLedger()` whose one `announce(profile)` reads **`resolveVisitorSchedule(profile)`**
  — the canonical resolver, untouched — and records each key in a `Set` **before** returning its cry.
  There is no second hash, no window arithmetic, no completion filter and no ordering of its own: the
  arrivals, their order and `completedVisitors` are whatever that resolver answers, and `seenVisitors` is
  never read, so being seen cannot suppress a call. Nothing is written anywhere: no profile field, no
  schema version, no migration, no `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`, no timer, no per-frame work, no mesh,
  prompt, collider, encounter, offer or price.

- **The wiring is one `useRef` and one `useEffect` in `App.tsx`.** `visitorHeraldRef` sits beside
  `heraldCries`; the effect is gated `if (currentScreen !== 'city_3d' || !profile || oathBeatMode) return;`
  with deps `[currentScreen, profile, oathBeatMode]`, and appends through the existing channel —
  `setHeraldCries((previous) => [...previous, ...cries])` — so `HeraldToast` is still the one surface and
  unrelated cries are preserved. Depending on `profile` (not on `enterCity`) is what announces a day
  turned while the city stays mounted: lodging (`handleLodging` sets a new profile literal) and a settled
  duel both re-run the effect, while a day whose arrivals were already called answers `[]`.

- **Dedup lifecycle, stated as behaviour.** One `(day, visitorId)` is called once per session: a
  re-render, an unrelated profile update, a city exit/re-entry on the same day and React StrictMode's
  double effect invocation are all silent; a later day is a new key and speaks again (day 15 announces
  both visitors, day 21 announces the bladesmith again). A **reload** announces the current day's
  arrivals once more — deliberate, documented, and the reason no `sessionStorage` was added: nothing in
  the source requires persistence for this cry, which is a presentation of a derived schedule.

- **Cry copy.** `The herald cries: Hanno of Cirta, the Wandering Bladesmith, walks the city today!` /
  `… Vibius the Campanian, the Itinerant Armorer …`. The suite asserts the name and title are present and
  that **no** day offer id, pool id, `offer.summary`, visitor id, `gold` or `finish_ventive` appears, so a
  rare item can never be spoiled by the announcement.

- **The three vacuous signage assertions are repaired, and the repair is shown to bite.**
  `src/utils/landmarkSignClearance.ts` (new, imports nothing, used by the tests only) replaces the clamped
  `Math.hypot(...) >= 0` idiom with the standard separating-axis test on **unclamped** separations:
  `rectsClear(a, b)` is true only when `max(bMinX − aMaxX, aMinX − bMaxX) > 0` or the same on Z —
  touching exactly (separation 0) is **not** clear. The three sites now use it:
  `l17bLandmarkSigns.test.ts` §C "every sign stands clear of every collider" (was `gapBetween(...) >= 0`),
  and `l17dLandmarkSignReliability.test.ts` §B (was `Math.hypot(dx, dz) >= 0`) and §D (the same). The
  measured own-building clearance band, every circle collider check, the segment checks, the hub/arrival
  distances and the flanking-facade `gapBetween` measurement are all unchanged — `gapBetween` survives for
  the distance it really measures, and no production collider, sign placement or registry value moved
  (still 142 colliders / 32 rectangles / 46 `colo-*` / 21 hubs / 21 arrivals).

- **The regression control, with measured evidence.** The Barracks sign clears `gladiator-barracks` by the

  mount **0.50 north** (local Z 3.6 → 3.1): the separations measure **x < 0** and **z = −0.149**, i.e. the
  footprint sits 0.149 inside the plinth's Z band and between its X sides. The shipped fixture is asserted

- **New suite: `src/utils/visitorHerald.test.ts` — 23 tests / 95 `expect()`.** §A determinism (fresh

## Scoped herald dismissal (L21D — implemented; runtime/visual acceptance PENDING)

- **Preflight.** Repo root `/app`, branch `development-focus-strategy`, HEAD
  **`a9246405a28eb7e1b9054df70188e7d19fe0da1c`** (`Implement L21B visitor arrival herald system`),
  `git status --short` empty and `git diff` empty. L21B is committed at that tip — it is not in the
  working tree and not split across commits. Nothing was reset, stashed, discarded, deployed, pushed
  or restarted; the L21C audit's HEAD was the same commit and its working tree was clean too.
  **The L21B record's own preflight line is left exactly as written** (it names `8c46411`, the tip
  that phase began on) because each record in this file states *its own* phase's baseline; editing it
  would misreport which commit the work was built on. L21B stands committed as `a924640`.

- **The defect, confirmed from the audit rather than assumed.** `HeraldToast` dismissed with
  `onDismiss={() => setHeraldCries([])}` — a **whole-queue replace** — while the L21B visitor ledger
  records its `(day, visitorId)` key *before* it returns the cry (`utils/visitorHerald.ts`, `called.add`
  ahead of `cries.push`). A cry appended between the toast's render and its dismissal landing (the
  seven-second timer of a stack that had grown, or a tap on a stack a newer cry had just joined) was
  destroyed with its key already spent, so that day's call was silently lost for the rest of the
  session. Both cry writers — the visitor effect and `evaluateRituals` — only ever APPEND, which is
  what makes the fix below exact.

- **The rule (`src/utils/heraldQueue.ts`, new, 46 lines, pure).** `removeDisplayedCries(queue,
  displayed)` removes exactly the cries a toast **displayed** from the front of the live queue and
  nothing else. Because the queue is append-only, the displayed snapshot is always a **prefix**, so a
  cry appended after that render stays queued and visible. It is deliberately **not** a blind
  `slice(displayed.length)`: every displayed position is compared first, and a queue that does not
  begin with the snapshot is returned **untouched** (a stale cry left up is a far smaller failure than
  deleting a newer one whose key is spent). It returns the **same array** when nothing matched, so
  React bails out. No storage, no React, no timer, no clock, no save field.

- **The wiring — two files, three call sites, no new state.** `HeraldToast` now takes
  `onDismiss: (displayed: readonly string[]) => void` and passes **the snapshot it rendered**, from
  both of its paths: the timer (`window.setTimeout(() => onDismiss(cries), durationMs)`) and the
  dismiss control (`onClick={() => onDismiss(cries)}`). `App` routes that through one stable handler,
  `const handleHeraldDismiss = useCallback((displayed) => setHeraldCries((previous) =>
  removeDisplayedCries(previous, displayed)), [])`, and the toast is mounted as
  `<HeraldToast cries={heraldCries} onDismiss={handleHeraldDismiss} />`. The stable identity is also
  the timer's dependency, so the seven seconds now run from the **last cry** rather than from the last
  App render (previously any App re-render restarted it); the 7 s `durationMs` default is unchanged.
  `heraldCries` remains the same `string[]` App state, so **the road-milestone channel
  (`[...previous, ...evaluation.cries]`), the visitor channel (`[...previous, ...cries]`), their copy,
  their order and the append semantics are untouched**, as are the visitor ledger, its keys, the
  StrictMode behaviour and the save schema. No new timer, no persistent state, no save field, no
  per-frame work; `App.tsx` gained one import of `useCallback` and one of the helper.

- **Regression suite: `src/utils/heraldQueue.test.ts` — 15 tests / 34 `expect()`**, covering the
  audit's five required cases plus the controls: §A snapshot removal (whole stack, leading snapshot);
  §B cries appended after the snapshot survive (one append, several); §C the old timer's callback
  firing after a newer cry arrives leaves it queued, and a **control** replays the pre-fix
  whole-queue clear and shows it losing that cry; §D consecutive/stale dismissals are no-ops and the
  re-rendered stack still dismisses; §E ordering preserved, empty dismissal and a non-prefix snapshot
  returning the **same array**, duplicate text dismissed once per displayed row; §F the toast itself —
  **rendered with `react-dom/server`** (the repo's convention; there is no DOM renderer or
  `@testing-library/react` here) asserting every cry in order, `role="status"`,
  `aria-live="polite"`, one labelled dismiss control per cry, and `''` for an empty queue, plus a
  narrow source pin of the two payload sites; §G App's wiring — the helper call, the absence of any
  `setHeraldCries([])`, the toast mount, both append lines and the untouched visitor ledger ref.
  App's queue is modelled as its real writers leave it (two functional appends), so every state
  transition the suite exercises is one App can actually perform.

- **Verified 2026-10-28** in the existing healthy `web` container (no restart, no rebuild): focused
  `bun test src/utils/heraldQueue.test.ts` → **15 pass / 0 fail** (34 expect); herald/road/signage
  `bun test src/utils/{visitorHerald,roadMilestones,roadOfGlory,l17bLandmarkSigns,l17dLandmarkSignReliability}.test.ts`
  → **125 pass / 0 fail** (4018 expect, 5 files — the L21B and L21C baselines intact, including
  `visitorHerald`'s §H wiring pins, which needed no change because the append line it pins is
  unchanged); `bun test` → **4112 pass / 0 fail (148 files, 174 390 expect() calls)** (L21B left
  4097 / 147; the delta is this suite's 15 tests and its file); `bun run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) →
  **exit 0**; `bun run build` → **exit 0** (the pre-existing >500 kB chunk warning only; startup
  assets ✓ 8/8); `git diff --check` → **clean**. Reviewed for scope: no change to visitor scheduling,
  profile mutation, save schema, cry copy or order, the 7 s duration, the road-milestone call sites,
  or `visitorHerald.ts` itself.

- **Not automatically verified — the live toast.** A cry (road milestone or visitor arrival) needs a
  save standing on a qualifying day or a settled duel, and this phase does not seed or fabricate one;
  the sandbox also renders the city hub at ~2 fps through SwiftShader. What could be checked is that
  the changed `App.tsx` still boots; **the dismissal race itself is covered by the suite's state
  transitions, not by a browser gesture**, and no visual or Android acceptance is claimed. Two
  remaining limitations worth knowing: (a) identity is (position, text), which is sufficient because
  each toast instance dismisses at most once — both of its paths fire once — so a snapshot is never
  reused against a queue that has since grown the same text again; (b) a day turned while the player
  is off `city_3d` and turned again before returning is still only announced for the day they stand
  in, which is L21B's documented behaviour and is unchanged here.

## Isolated visitor-herald runtime harness (L21M — implemented; browser-verified; committed `56d6b7a`)

- **Final committed state (verified by L21O).** The implementation is **committed as
  `56d6b7ac56728ec4bcdaf7f50ec09dd4c3d581cc`** — *Implement L21M herald dev harness and diagnostics*,
  4 files with **+907 / −0** (`HeraldHarness.tsx` and its suite new, one gate constant plus one branch
  in `src/main.tsx`, this record) — and that commit is **pushed**: HEAD and
  `origin/development-focus-strategy` are the same commit, 0 ahead / 0 behind, working tree clean. The
  L21M work below is therefore history, not an uncommitted tree.

- **Preflight as recorded at the time (historical — the tree was uncommitted then).** Branch
  `development-focus-strategy`, HEAD **`c02d5b81e91314f9a4d338ce218fdf0e887abaea`**, `git status
  --porcelain` empty and the working tree clean *before* L21M's files were written; `docker compose ps`
  showed `app-web-1` `running (healthy)` and `curl localhost:3000/` answered **200** — the running
  `web` container was not restarted, rebuilt or otherwise touched. Nothing was reset, stashed,
  discarded, committed, pushed or deployed during that phase; the commit above is the platform's
  end-of-turn commit, made afterwards.

- **Why a harness instead of a test.** L21B (the herald calls the day's visitors) and L21D (a dismissal
  removes only what the toast displayed) are pinned by pure suites, but the cry had never been read off
  a screen: it only exists while the 3D city hub is mounted on a day the schedule resolves, and this
  sandbox renders that hub at a few frames per second — reaching an arrival day by playing means
  fabricating a save, which risks the player's progress. L21M adds a disposable diagnostic route and
  nothing else.

- **The route.** `?devHarness=herald`, plus the repo's existing dev-only scratch flag
  `sand_and_steel_dev_harness = 'herald'`, behind the same `import.meta.env.DEV &&` gate every other
  harness uses. `src/main.tsx` gained one gate constant and one `} else if (useHeraldHarness) {` branch
  that dynamically imports the component and mounts it **instead of** `<App />`; the branch sits before
  the app fallback, so the title screen, the save loader and the city hub never run. The component
  self-guards with `if (!import.meta.env.DEV) return null;`.

- **`src/components/dev/HeraldHarness.tsx` (new, ~391 lines) — everything it shows is production.**
  (1) The profile is a minimal fixture `{ city: { day: 5 } }` held in component state; the module does
  **not** import `services/storage` at all, so `loadSavedProfile` / `saveProfile` /
  `PROFILE_STORAGE_KEY` are unreachable rather than merely unused. (2) Arrivals come from
  `resolveVisitorSchedule(profile)`, and the panel **reports** whether that answer contains
  `numidian_bladesmith` instead of asserting him. (3) The first cry comes from
  `createVisitorHeraldLedger().announce(profile)` — no cry text exists in the component's source.
  (4) The toast is the shipping `HeraldToast`, handed the live queue and an `onDismiss` that is the
  production `removeDisplayedCries` helper (same snapshot semantics as `App.handleHeraldDismiss`).
  (5) The second cry is a **second** real ledger's answer for the first later day the schedule resolves
  anyone (day 8 today — walked by `resolveSecondCry`, never hard-coded), because the L21B ledger is
  one-shot per `(day, visitorId)`. (6) "Dismiss previous snapshot" hands the stack the toast rendered
  **before** the append to the same production dismissal path — the exact L21D stale-snapshot case — so
  the newer cry stays queued and is then what the toast shows. (7) Reset clears only
  `HERALD_HARNESS_KEY` and the in-memory run, then re-emits through a fresh ledger. The toast uses
  `durationMs = 60_000` so a human can drive the two steps; the dismissal path is the component's own
  `onDismiss(cries)` either way.

- **Storage isolation.** The only storage the harness touches is the new scratch key
  `HERALD_HARNESS_KEY = 'sand_and_steel_herald_harness_v1'` (sessionStorage first, localStorage only as
  a fallback), holding `{ day, firstCry }` — what this tab last emitted. No game-save key is read,
  written, migrated or cleared, and nothing calls `sessionStorage.clear()` / `localStorage.clear()`.
  Measured live after a full run: `sessionStorage` held exactly `sand_and_steel_herald_harness_v1` (plus
  the platform's own `__b44_seed_applied`) and `localStorage` was **empty** — the save key
  `sand_and_steel_gladiator_save_v2` never appeared.

- **New suite: `src/utils/l21mHeraldHarness.test.ts` — 19 tests / 93 `expect()`.** §A the route (the

## Gold/NaN — one reader of the purse (implemented)

- **Symptom.** Straight after a fight, the result screen's **"Purse Now"** row read **"NaN Gold"**, and
  from then on so did the city hub's purse chip, the shop, the workshop, the pre-race panel and the
  academy header — the `NaN` was in the save. Nothing threw: the figure is only ever *printed*.
- **Root cause, measured on the shipped code.** Gold was never normalized at any boundary.
  `loadSavedProfile` returned `JSON.parse(raw)` untouched, so a profile whose `gold` is missing or
  unusable (an older schema, a hand-edited file, a cloud save from another build) carried
  `undefined`. App's victory settlement then computed `base.gold + stats.goldEarned` → **`NaN`**, which
  was written into `updatedProfile` and `saveProfile`d, so every later read was `NaN` too. The result
  screen's guard was `typeof goldTotal === 'number'`, which **`NaN` satisfies**, so the row rendered the
  broken figure instead of hiding it. (The arena purse itself was already NaN-safe:
  `calculateDuelGold` clamps every input through `toCount`.)
- **The fix — one helper, four boundaries, no new behaviour.**
  - `src/utils/currency.ts` (new) — `normalizeGold(value)`: a finite number passes through unchanged
    (never re-rounded), anything else (`NaN`, `±Infinity`, `undefined`, `null`, a string, `true`, an
    object) reads as `0`, and a negative purse is floored at `0`. It is the ONE reader, in the same
    spirit as `normalizeInjury` for the injury slot.
  - `src/services/storage.ts` — `loadSavedProfile` normalizes `gold` on the way in (and returns `null`
    for a JSON value that is not a record, instead of spreading a primitive). A valid purse is
    untouched, and the read still writes nothing.
  - `src/App.tsx` — the victory credit is now
    `normalizeGold(base.gold) + normalizeGold(stats.goldEarned)`, so a victory pays its own purse
    instead of poisoning the save. This also closes the documented gate issue (a `NaN` purse passed
    every `gold < price` comparison) at the source, without touching a single gate.
  - `src/services/googleDrive.ts` — `loadProfileFromDrive` normalizes at the same boundary, so a cloud
    restore cannot reintroduce an unusable purse.
  - `src/components/hub/DuelResultModal.tsx` — the "Purse Now" guard is `Number.isFinite(goldTotal)`
    instead of `typeof goldTotal === 'number'`, so the row is withheld rather than printed wrong.
- **Regression suite: `src/utils/currency.test.ts`** — 13 tests / 43 assertions. §A the reader's
  contract; §B the **rendered** result screen (`react-dom/server`, the repo's convention for a repo
  with no DOM test library): a `NaN` purse prints no "NaN" and no "Purse Now", a real purse still reads
  "135 Gold", an absent purse keeps the row out; §C the wiring — the exact credit expression, and a
  save whose `gold` is `undefined` / `null` / `"120"` / `true` loading as `0` while the rest of the
  record is untouched and the stored bytes are not rewritten. Plus **§H in
  `duelSettlementCommit.test.ts`**, which executes App's OWN `handleMatchComplete` source: a profile
  with `gold` missing settles to exactly the fight's purse (90), the saved object is finite, a purse
  already poisoned with `NaN` is healed the same way, and an intact 500 still becomes 590.
- **Before / after, verbatim.** The suite was run against the unfixed tree first: **8 pass / 5 fail**
  (the rendered "NaN Gold", the guard, the credit, the load boundary and the cloud boundary), then
  **13 pass / 0 fail** after the fix. Nothing was weakened to get there.
- **Rebased, not weakened (test-only):** `duelRewards.test.ts` and `duelResultLifecycle.test.ts` pinned
  the bare credit expression and now pin the normalized one, each with a comment naming this change;
  `duelSettlementCommit.test.ts` and `arenaReachability.test.ts` **execute App's handler source** and
  therefore had to be handed the shipped `normalizeGold` as a `new Function` parameter (without it the
  executed handler threw `ReferenceError`, which is what those two suites caught).
- **Verified 2026-10-28** in the existing healthy `web` container (no restart): `bun test` over the 41
  files that touch the changed modules (`storage`, `App`, `DuelResultModal`, `googleDrive` — every
  suite that names `loadSavedProfile`, `handleMatchComplete`, `goldTotal` or executes App's source) →
  **1152 pass / 0 fail / 10778 expect() calls**; `bun run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) → **exit 0**;
  `git diff --check` → clean.
- **Not automatically verified, and why.** (a) The **in-game** purse readout was not observed in the
  sandbox browser: this environment clears `localStorage` on a full document load, so a seeded
  corrupt save cannot be re-hydrated for a visual check (the same limit recorded for earlier preview
  work). (b) No duel was fought, so the credit was exercised by executing App's real handler source,
  not by playing a bout at the hub's ~2 fps. (c) Android remains outstanding for every screen. The
  display guard itself **is** verified by rendering the real component.

  "L22"` matched only `bun.lock` and binaries; nothing in `/tmp` or `.base44/*.md`), and no run log or
  capture survived. Nothing from the earlier session was recoverable, so **every check below was
  reproduced in this phase**, not recovered.
- **Starting state.** `development-focus-strategy` at `ebc39d65dc`, 0 ahead / 0 behind
  `origin/development-focus-strategy`, `git status --short` empty.
- **Historical Git metadata issue (not a functional defect).** `ebc39d6`'s message reads "Mark
  inconclusive URL check as skipped instead of retrying", but its diff is a single hunk: the L17B signage
  guidance correction (`AGENTS.md` +30 / -7). The message describes a change that commit does not
  contain; it is left as committed, and the signage figures it *does* carry were recomputed from source
  and confirmed by the L22A audit.
